stories.title: 12 ways Ann Arbor plans to divide and spend millions from downtown property sale

The sale is expected to close in 2027, with the final amount depending on the number of housing units developed.

stories.title: 19-year-old charged in crash that killed Uber driver, injured passenger in Oak Park
stories.summary: Tracy Darwin Sutton, 19, was charged after allegedly driving through a traffic light in Oak Park, causing a crash that killed an Uber driver and injured a passenger. The incident occurred on September 17, with Sutton found intoxicated. The Uber driver died in the hospital, while the 23-year-old passenger remains in critical condition. Sutton was arraigned on September 20 with a $2 million bond and is scheduled for a court appearance on September 28.

stories.title: A Data Center on the Huron River: Ypsilanti Township Pushes Back
stories.summary: A proposed $1.25 billion research computing center by the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory on a 144-acre site along the Huron River in Ypsilanti Township faces significant community opposition. Residents and local officials have raised concerns about environmental impact, water and energy use, and the lack of transparency in the project's planning. Ypsilanti City Council imposed a 60-day moratorium on data center construction, and community protests continue as the university and local government debate the project's future.

If approved on Nov. 3, the city would establish a public utility board by 2028 to oversee a potential transition. The proposal faces opposition from DTE-funded groups, but court challenges to block it have been dismissed. Supporters argue for democratic control and reliability, while critics highlight potential high costs and grid maintenance concerns.

With state funding stagnant and tuition pressures, universities are struggling to maintain operations, according to the Michigan Association of State Universities. The situation could result in significant job cuts and reduced economic activity across the state.

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities

With shrinking student numbers and stagnant state aid, regional universities are struggling to maintain operations, affecting local economies through reduced employment and spending.

stories.title: As Michigan reading scores fall, state superintendent says: ‘We need to improve.’
stories.summary: Michigan's third grade reading proficiency rates show significant gaps between economically disadvantaged and non-disadvantaged students, with the former lagging by more than half. Districts like Detroit and Grand Rapids reported modest gains in reading and math, while others like Ypsilanti saw mixed results. State officials emphasize the need for improved attendance, curriculum updates, and community partnerships to address declining performance.

photo.alt: As Michigan reading scores fall, state superintendent says: ‘We need to improve.’

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit revealed that $59 million of Michigan's workforce training funds were used for employer on-the-job training reimbursements instead of education to boost worker skills. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax oversight and documentation, with the state contesting the findings. The report highlights misaligned spending against program goals and calls for improved compliance.

photo.alt: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent

stories.title: Audit finds fault in Michigan job training program, claims $59M misspent
stories.summary: A state audit found that one-third of $182.5 million in Michigan's Going Pro Talent Fund was spent on new hire orientation instead of education to boost worker skills and wages. The audit criticized the Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity for lax documentation and oversight, while the state disputed the findings, defending on-the-job training as a valid upskilling method. The 2027 budget for the program is $14.4 million, a 40% decline from the previous year.

stories.title: Bloomfield's New Home Repair Loan Program to Open Soon: What to Know

Applications open on October 6, with income limits set at 80% of regional median income. The program, approved by the township council on September 14, 2026, prioritizes health and safety improvements and offers no-interest, forgivable loans. Office hours for residents are scheduled for September 30 and October 7, with projects expected to begin in December.

The Hannahville Tribal Police Department responded to the scene and began lifesaving measures before the child was transported to a hospital.

stories.title: Carbon capture proposals draw mixed responses from environmental groups in Michigan House committee
stories.summary: Michigan's House Energy Committee considered bills to establish a state framework for carbon capture, utilization, and sequestration. While supporters like Rep. stories.title: Community
stories.summary: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free. At Greendale Community College, all are accepted and all have a bright future ahead of them. Have you ever felt nervous to deliver a class presentation in front of dozens of strangers? Have you ever been humbled by what you thought would be a blowoff class? Have you ever been helpless to stop petty bickering between close friends? There’s a “Community” episode for each of these issues, and many more. The show captured viewers’ attention with ambitious outings, like “[Modern Warfare](https://youtu.be/XcOG5iZpV-k?si=7RcOVN8nPRSMI8Va)” (a paintball competition set entirely at the college) and “[Remedial Chaos Theory](https://youtu.be/POT3plx0vBs?si=bwUHzhUT4ThVsHjt)” (a timeline-hopping adventure of what-ifs). But in its golden years — specifically Seasons 1-3 — “Community” thrived on its warm relatability and sympathy for a band of misfits [bound together](https://youtu.be/aznTfytzNQ4?si=UXdGH1eh7y_7D85K) by [mutual](https://youtu.be/q44WaM5Rm6A?si=3vzWloDJtpF5duut) [lunacy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dlXuJpuk6oA): the “Study Group.’’ The members of the group are all at different stages of life, but ultimately seeking the same thing: a raw, unadulterated college experience and all the insight it might bring. “Community” is anchored by inventive, witty sitcom writing and a set of comedic powerhouses delivering career-best performances. If you’re in college, there’s never been a better time to watch it.

photo.alt: Courtesy of Ana Torresarpi

Repeal efforts are underway but face challenges in a GOP-controlled Congress.

photo.alt: Democrats, experts call for revocation of school voucher program under adoption by states

stories.title: Demolition begins on historic Roseville church to make way for Sheetz gas station
stories.summary: Crews began demolishing the former Sacred Heart Church in Roseville on Sept. 21 to make way for a new Sheetz gas station. The church, which closed in 2017 after 156 years, was replaced by an $8 million development that sparked reactions from residents. Demolition is expected to take six to eight weeks, with construction starting this fall and the station opening next year.

photo.alt: Former Sacred Heart Church at Gratiot and Utica in the process of demolition on Sept. 22, 2026.

stories.title: Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy Receives $671 Million Appropriation
stories.summary: The Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy will receive $671.4 million for fiscal year 2026-2027. The appropriation includes 1,641 full-time positions and funds for environmental programs and services.

stories.title: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's Department of Public Safety is hosting bike registration events for students. Students who use bikes on campus must register them with the department to ensure safety and track ownership.

photo.alt: Students registering bikes at Eastern Michigan University

stories.title: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students
stories.summary: Eastern Michigan University's Department of Public Safety is hosting free bike and scooter registration events for students on Sept. 15 and Sept. 21. Registration requires personal information, vehicle details, and serial numbers, with participants receiving identification stickers and an ID number to aid in recovery if stolen. The first three registrants at each event will receive a free U-lock.

photo.alt: Department of Public Safety hosts bike registration events for students

stories.title: Department Required to Report Land Transactions by December 1
stories.summary: The department must submit a report by December 1 on all land transactions completed in the prior fiscal year, including parcel details, location, transaction amounts, fund sources, and types.

stories.title: Department Required to Submit Training Models Report by December 1
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services must submit a report by December 1 listing training models approved for use in licensed child caring institutions, as required by the Michigan Administrative Code.

stories.title: Destination Stars Hollow
stories.summary: Destination Stars Hollow, conceived by Laura Boote and Kathleen London, transforms downtown Brighton into the quaint little hamlet of Stars Hollow on September 26-27, 2026. General admission is free, but Meet & Greet tickets with Patterson and Gunn cost $75/actor, and a Q&A with Bishop about her time on 'Gilmore Girls' costs $100.

photo.alt: Destination Stars Hollow

stories.title: Detroit Action Hires Electoral Canvasser for Voter Registration
stories.summary: Detroit Action is hiring people to talk to residents about current issues and voter registration for November’s general election. Canvassers are paid $22 an hour.

stories.title: Detroit Action Hires Electoral Canvassers for November General Election
stories.summary: Detroit Action is hiring canvassers to discuss current issues and voter registration for the November general election. The role pays $22/hour.

stories.title: Detroit and Flint teens struggle with mental health – and worried adults around them feel 'helpless'
stories.summary: Teens in Detroit and Flint face mental health challenges, with adults feeling helpless. Programs focusing on safe spaces, school staff training, and community involvement are being developed. Teens emphasize the need for supportive environments, mentorship, and strength-based approaches.

photo.alt: Young women cheer and clap. Spaces that affirm teens’ identities can support well-being. Brynn Anderson/AP

stories.title: Detroit asks residents to help identify historic places worth preserving
stories.summary: Detroit is seeking community input to identify and protect historic sites through the Preserve Detroit initiative. Residents can submit photos, addresses, and stories about significant locations, with a focus on preserving sites tied to the city's diverse history and preventing demolition without public discussion.

photo.alt: Detroit asks residents to help identify historic places worth preserving

stories.title: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance
stories.summary: Detroit charter schools show significant disparities in student proficiency rates, with some schools improving reading and writing scores through initiatives like AP courses, while math performance remains low. For example, Voyageur Academy had 9.9% third-grade reading proficiency, while Detroit Edison Public School Academy reached 50.5%. Jalen Rose Leadership Academy increased SAT reading/writing benchmarks from 13.3% to 38.5% since 2018-19.

photo.alt: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance

stories.title: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance
stories.summary: Detroit charter schools show significant variation in student proficiency rates, with some schools improving reading and writing scores through initiatives like AP courses, while others struggle with low math performance. For example, Voyageur Academy had only 9.9% of third graders at reading proficiency, while Detroit Edison Public School Academy reached 50.5%. Jalen Rose Leadership Academy improved SAT reading/writing benchmarks from 13.3% to 38.5% since 2018-19, but math scores remain low at 6%.

photo.alt: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance

stories.title: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance
stories.summary: Detroit charter schools show significant disparities in student proficiency rates, with some schools like Voyageur Academy having only 9.9% of third graders at or above reading proficiency, while others like Detroit Edison Public School Academy reach 50.5%. Jalen Rose Leadership Academy has improved reading and writing scores through AP courses, but math performance remains low. Newer charters like KIPP Detroit Imani Academy are working to meet proficiency goals.

photo.alt: Detroit charter schools have big gaps in performance

stories.title: Detroit City Council Envisions Fort Wayne's Future with Community Focus
stories.summary: Detroit City Council Member Gabriela Santiago-Romero emphasizes accessibility, cultural programming, and community access for Fort Wayne's revitalization. She highlights the need for amenities like coffee shops and gift shops, along with partnerships to create a vibrant public space. The vision draws inspiration from collaborative models like Ralph Wilson Park and the Joe Louis Greenway.

photo.alt: Detroit City Council Envisions Fort Wayne's Future with Community Focus

stories.title: Detroit Disability Power Hires Communications and Design Coordinator
stories.summary: Detroit Disability Power is hiring a visual artist to expand its reach and create accessible graphics for social media, email, print and online spaces. The full-time position pays a salary of $55,000-$62,000 plus benefits. Apply by Sept. 23.

photo.alt: Outlier Media Building

stories.title: Detroit district catching up to charter schools, 2026 M-STEP results show
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) showed long-term growth in 2026 M-STEP results but lagged behind statewide averages in student proficiency. Charter schools like Pembroke Academy outperformed both DPSCD and state benchmarks, with over 56% of third graders meeting reading proficiency compared to 44% statewide and 14.1% in DPSCD. Officials noted challenges in comparing charters and traditional districts due to differing student cohorts and systemic issues like poverty and racism.

photo.alt: Detroit district catching up to charter schools, 2026 M-STEP results show

stories.title: Detroit Election Commission handles business in 2-minute meeting
stories.summary: The Detroit Election Commission conducted all its business in a record 2-minute meeting, raising questions about the efficiency of November’s election preparations.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Detroit ethics board seeks independent counsel for Conrad Mallett probe
stories.summary: The Detroit Board of Ethics is working to secure independent legal counsel to investigate Corporation Counsel Conrad Mallett, who earned $1.8 million from Lear Corp. while approving a $4 million tax break for the company. A three-member panel will select an attorney for the investigation.

photo.alt: Detroit ethics board seeks independent counsel for Conrad Mallett probe

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Comerica Park receives a new name
stories.summary: Comerica Park, home of the Detroit Tigers, will be renamed Fifth Third Park after Fifth Third Bancorp acquired Comerica Bank. The name change, effective next year, follows the bank's rebranding of all branch locations. Michigan Regional President Steve Davis emphasized the significance of the park to Detroit's community pride.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: Comerica Park receives a new name

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Companies give seniors produce boxes to promote brain health on Alzheimer’s Day
stories.summary: Eli Lilly and Company and Planet Harvest are distributing over 1,300 brain-healthy produce boxes to food-insecure seniors in Metro Detroit on World Alzheimer’s Day. The boxes include apples, cabbage, cucumbers, collard greens, lemons, oranges, corn, and zucchinis. Seniors can pick up boxes at locations like Rochester Christian University and Webster Community Center, with door-to-door distributions at senior living homes.

photo.alt: Seniors receiving produce boxes to support brain health

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Kamala Harris endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit
stories.summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris endorsed Democrat Abdul El-Sayed for U.S. Senate at an event in Detroit. She highlighted his potential as a national voice for the state. El-Sayed addressed concerns from Arab and Muslim voters who previously supported Trump or minor candidates due to Biden administration policies on Israel.

photo.alt: Detroit Evening Report: Kamala Harris endorses Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: MDHHS to award $1.5 million for community violence intervention initiatives
stories.summary: Five organizations, including two in Detroit, will receive $1.5 million in funding from the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) for community violence intervention efforts. The grants aim to reduce firearm violence and its adverse outcomes in historically disinvested neighborhoods through public health and safety initiatives. Each organization will receive $300,000 for a two-year project running from September 1, 2026, to September 30, 2028.

photo.alt: Detroit's skyline from Belle Isle on November 16, 2023

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: Nonprofit LGBT Detroit provides mental health services at new facility on the city’s West side
stories.summary: LGBT Detroit Health, a nonprofit, is opening a new wellness center on Detroit's West side offering mental health services, fitness classes, and chronic care management. The facility provides a safe space for the LGBT community and partners with local health organizations for testing and vaccinations. It is funded through state grants and membership fees.

photo.alt: Image from WDET 101.9 FM

stories.title: Detroit Evening Report: ShotStoppers program significantly decreased gun violence, says University of Michigan report
stories.summary: A University of Michigan analysis found a 45% decrease in homicides and nonfatal shootings in Detroit since the launch of the ShotStoppers community violence intervention program three years ago. The program funds community-based organizations with $175,000 per quarter and performance-based bonuses to reduce gun violence in high-risk areas.

photo.alt: Image from WDET 101.9 FM

stories.title: Detroit explores alternatives to DTE Energy monopoly
stories.summary: Detroit City Council and Mayor Mary Sheffield's administration are investigating alternatives to DTE Energy's near-monopoly as the city's energy provider. Council members criticized frequent power outages and rate hikes, requesting a report on how other municipalities have diversified energy sources.

photo.alt: Detroit explores alternatives to DTE Energy monopoly

stories.title: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing
stories.summary: The family of Kimberlly Moore claims her body was accidentally cremated before her scheduled viewing at Hutchison Funeral Home, leading to a demand for answers. The funeral home has launched an internal investigation and stated they will address the issue if found at fault.

photo.alt: Detroit family says woman was mistakenly cremated before funeral viewing

stories.title: Detroit Farm and Cider owner sells property after legal disputes
stories.summary: Leandra King, owner of Detroit Farm and Cider, is selling her property for $5.3 million after years of legal disputes with the city over animal possession and code violations. The city recently seized animals from the property.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Detroit Forecast: Cool temps, rain chance ahead
stories.summary: Southeast Michigan will experience cooler-than-normal temperatures through mid-week with a slight chance of light showers Wednesday. High pressure will keep conditions dry through the weekend before warming into the lower 70s. The next significant rain is expected no earlier than mid-next week.

photo.alt: Cool weather continues with warming trend into the weekend. Graphic by National Weather Service.

stories.title: Detroit is Unrivaled presented by Ally
stories.summary: Detroit is Unrivaled presented by Ally is set for September 14, 2026. The event is part of a series of announcements from 313 Presents, including Trans-Siberian Orchestra's 30th Anniversary Winter Tour on December 23, 2026.

stories.title: Detroit Lions Day at the Zoo features Roary the mascot
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions will host a special event at the Detroit Zoo on September 20, 2026, with their mascot Roary meeting fans. The event is part of the Lions' community outreach initiatives.

photo.alt: Roary the Detroit Lions mascot will be on hand during the Detroit Lions Day at the Zoo, Sat. Sept. 20, 2026 to meet fans. (Photo courtesy of the Detroit Zoo Facebook page)

stories.title: Detroit man charged with murder in ‘random’ stabbing of Chipotle worker
stories.summary: A 42-year-old Detroit man, Devon Jason Watson, has been charged with first-degree murder in the fatal stabbing of 34-year-old Chipotle employee Jaquoya Wix. Prosecutors described the attack as random but premeditated. Watson and Wix did not know each other, and the stabbing occurred in an alley behind a downtown Detroit restaurant on Sept. 20, 2026.

stories.title: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield declines comment on OIG investigation into Bettison call with activist
stories.summary: Detroit Mayor Mary Sheffield declined to comment on an Office of Inspector General investigation into a recorded call between Police Chief Todd Bettison and activist Jahdante Smith. The call, recorded in August, involved Bettison asking Smith to remove social media posts featuring old photos of Sheffield. Sheffield stated the matter is under investigation and urged allowing the process to proceed without comment.

stories.summary: Detroit Month of Design provides residents with opportunities to shape the city’s future through events and projects. The newsletter highlights ways to get involved in urban design and community development.

stories.title: Detroit opens new round of home repair grants
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of Detroit homes need repairs, with a cost estimate of over $1 billion. The city has launched a new round of grants through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs, expected to repair around 250 homes. Applications are online-only, creating barriers for residents without internet access.

photo.alt: Ceiling with plaster and drywall damage exposes wooden joists and lath.

stories.title: Detroit parents, community members want change
stories.summary: Detroit parents and community members are calling for a new school board to challenge the status quo, emphasizing the need for faster academic progress, increased accountability, and broader measures of student success beyond graduation rates. Stakeholders like Jasmine Johnson, Gwen Moore, and Cyekeia Lee highlight the urgency for systemic improvements and collaboration between schools and families.

photo.alt: Detroit parents, community members want change

stories.title: Detroit Police Commissioner rescinds virtual public comment ban
stories.summary: Detroit Police Commissioner Henrietta Ivey rescinded her motion to ban virtual public comments at Board of Police Commissioners meetings following public outcry. The board shortened public comment time to 90 seconds and prioritized accessibility for people with disabilities.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools and DFT Reach Tentative Agreement on Class Size Overage Pay for 2026-2028
stories.summary: A tentative agreement between Detroit Public Schools Community District and the Detroit Federation of Teachers outlines new class size overage compensation for the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 school years. The agreement replaces existing formulas with specific class size targets, including thresholds for K-3, 4-5, 6-12, and special education classifications, and expires on June 30, 2028.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools and DFT Tentative Agreement Expires in 2028
stories.summary: A tentative agreement between Detroit Public Schools Community District and the Detroit Federation of Teachers (DFT) outlines terms for occupational therapists' caseloads, overage supplemental payments, and a June 30, 2028 expiration date. The agreement specifies quarterly payments for overage supplements, with the final payment due by the second July paycheck. Provisions of the existing DFT collective bargaining agreement remain in effect beyond this letter.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools Tentative Agreement 2026-2028: Teacher Payments for Oversized Classes
stories.summary: The tentative agreement outlines payment structures for teachers in Detroit Public Schools when class sizes exceed contractual maximums. Payments vary based on the number of students above the limit, with amounts per quarter and annual totals specified. Conditions include mutual acknowledgment of oversized classes and efforts to reduce enrollments.

stories.title: Detroit Public Schools to Allow PD Days for Bilingual Education
stories.summary: The tentative agreement allows teachers to use one of three designated Professional Development Days for training specific to the Office of Bilingual Education and Related Programs, as determined by the District’s Office of Curriculum and Instruction.

stories.title: Detroit reports 101 properties damaged after EF-2 tornado
stories.summary: Detroit’s storm response update shows 101 properties damaged by the Sept. 3 EF-2 tornado — the city’s first since 1997 — with the hardest-hit areas including McDougall-Hunt, Islandview, West Village, Indian Village, East Village, Pingree Park and Belle Isle. Mayor Mary Sheffield declared a local state of emergency. Crews removed 295 fallen trees, cleared 83 streets, hauled 342 tons of debris, and restored power to all traffic signals, though full recovery is expected to take time.

photo.alt: Detroit reports 101 properties damaged after EF-2 tornado

stories.title: Detroit's New Home Repair Grants Aim to Address $1 Billion Problem
stories.summary: Detroit has opened a new round of grants to repair homes, targeting around 250 properties through the Critical Home Repair and LeadSafe Housing programs. The preapplication process is online, creating barriers for residents without internet access, though a helpline is available for assistance. The city acknowledges the need for a more accessible system.

photo.alt: Detroit's New Home Repair Grants Aim to Address $1 Billion Problem

stories.title: Detroit school board appoints 25-year-old youth advocate as its newest member
stories.summary: Jeremiah Steen, a 25-year-old philanthropist and youth advocate, was appointed to the Detroit Public Schools Community District board to fill a vacancy left by the death of Iris Taylor. He will serve until December 2026 and plans to focus on workforce development and economic mobility for students.

photo.alt: Jeremiah Steen answers the board's questions in an interview for the position. (Hannah Dellinger / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit School Board Election Features 34 Candidates for 5 Seats
stories.summary: The Detroit Public School Community District school board election will see 34 candidates competing for five open seats. Only 19 of the 34 candidates responded to Chalkbeat Detroit's outreach about their priorities and views on district challenges. Voters will choose among them on November 3.

photo.alt: Detroit School Board Election Features 34 Candidates for 5 Seats

stories.title: Detroit school board’s chair and vice chair will not seek reelection in November
stories.summary: Two Detroit school board leaders, LaTrice McClendon and Corletta Vaughn, will not seek reelection in November, leading to a potential shift in the district's direction. McClendon was disqualified due to a late fee her campaign team missed, while Vaughn owed fees to Wayne County. Their absence may affect Superintendent Nikolai Vitti's administrative agenda.

photo.alt: DPSCD board chair LaTrice McClendon, left, and vice chair Corletta Vaughn, are not running for reelection. They are shown in a June 2025 meeting reading a statement about a district student who had been detained by federal immigration officials.

stories.title: Detroit school board signals desire to find alternatives to demolition for four closed buildings
stories.summary: The Detroit school board is reconsidering plans to demolish four recently closed schools after facing community criticism. Originally slated for demolition in June 2027, the board is now exploring alternatives like selling or leasing the buildings. Community members and some board members argue that repurposing the sites could generate funds for classrooms instead of spending nearly $5 million on demolition.

photo.alt: Some board members for the Detroit Public Schools Community District are reconsidering plans to demolish four school buildings that closed at the end of the 2025-26 school year. (Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat)

stories.title: Detroit school board to fill vacant seat of late member Iris Taylor ahead of November election
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District board must fill a vacant seat left by the late Iris Taylor within 30 days of state law, with interviews for two candidates beginning as early as next week. The selected appointee will serve through the end of 2026, and the process includes Sherisse Butler, the 2024 election runner-up, among others.

photo.alt: Board members meet to interview candidates in July 2025

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy to restrict unexcused early sign-outs, requiring documentation for pickups and prohibiting early releases in the final 30 minutes of the school day. Parents will face mandatory meetings and attendance contracts if their children accumulate multiple unexcused departures, with consequences including chronic absenteeism tracking and potential grade repetition.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit school district has adopted a new policy to address unexcused early sign-outs, with parents expressing mixed reactions. While some support protecting instructional time, others raise concerns about socioeconomic barriers and the needs of students with disabilities. The district acknowledges limited research on partial-day absenteeism and its impact on learning.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) has implemented a new policy to address partial-day absenteeism by curbing unexcused early sign-outs. Parents expressed mixed reactions, with some supporting the change to protect instructional time and others raising concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. The district highlights the issue similarly to its efforts against chronic absenteeism, though limited research exists on effective solutions for partial-day absences.

photo.alt: Detroit school district adopts new policy to curb unexcused early sign-outs

stories.title: Detroit school district releases 2026-27 calendar
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District has released its 2026-27 school year calendar, with a start date of Aug. 24 for students. The calendar includes 175 student attendance days and five professional development days for staff, meeting Michigan's 180-day minimum. It does not observe Eid al-Fitr, a Muslim holiday expected on March 10, despite advocacy from students and community members.

photo.alt: Detroit school district releases 2026-27 calendar

stories.title: Detroit school district’s tax proposal gets voter approval
stories.summary: Detroit Public Schools' operating millage proposal, which needed voter approval by July 2027, has been approved. The tax applies to commercial, rental, and vacation properties but not primary residences. The approval avoids potential November elections if the proposal had failed.

photo.alt: Detroit school district’s tax proposal gets voter approval

stories.title: Detroit students canvass to ask voters to support Proposal S
stories.summary: Detroit students and volunteers with 482Forward are canvassing to promote Proposal S, a school millage on the Aug. 4 primary ballot that would allow Detroit Public Schools Community District to collect its own operating tax. If not approved by July 1, 2027, the district faces an $111 million deficit. The campaign aims to educate voters about the millage, which replaces a previous system and ensures continued funding for schools.

photo.alt: Lindsey Matson, deputy director of youth organizing for 482Forward, explains Proposal S to a voter in Corktown.

stories.title: Detroit Tenants Union Lawsuit: Evictions and Compliance
stories.summary: The Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit challenges eviction practices tied to housing compliance, with landlords warning of market collapse due to maintenance costs and tenants arguing safety shouldn't depend on profitability. The next hearing is set for Sept. 21, where a judge may rule on a motion to dismiss the case.

photo.alt: A row of older red-brick-and-wood houses with porches and trees line the street under a gray, overcast sky.

stories.title: Detroit to Receive $1.25M for Right-to-Counsel Eviction Program
stories.summary: The city of Detroit in Wayne County will receive $1.25 million to implement a right-to-counsel program for tenants facing eviction proceedings. This initiative aims to provide legal support to city tenants during eviction processes.

stories.title: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.
stories.summary: The Avenue of Fashion is highlighted as a test case for expanding retail in Detroit's neighborhoods. Surrounding areas like Sherwood Forest and Palmer Woods contribute to the corridor's potential, with existing businesses such as Bakers Keyboard Lounge adding to its appeal. Strategies include increasing year-round activity through winter events and holiday shopping to boost foot traffic beyond the summer season.

photo.alt: Detroit wants more retail in its neighborhoods. Small businesses say they need more foot traffic first.

stories.title: Detroit woman facing human trafficking, prostitution charges after victim seeks help from motel housekeeper
stories.summary: A Detroit woman has been charged with operating a human trafficking enterprise in Southfield after an alleged prostitution victim sought help from a motel housekeeper. Prosecutors say the victim was lured into prostitution by Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, and was forced to perform sex acts. The victim approached a housekeeper at the Marvins Garden Inn on Sept. 10, prompting police to be contacted and Robinson to be arrested.

photo.alt: Janeice Florence Robinson, 27, of Detroit, is facing multiple felony charges for allegedly trafficking a woman into prostitution at a Southfield motel.

stories.title: Detroit woman’s basement floods with sewage after city pipe work
stories.summary: Detroit resident Sharon Poindexter has dealt with sewage backing up into her basement since around Sept. 10, coinciding with city crews replacing lead service lines on her street. She says the situation worsens whenever her household uses water and that repeated calls to the city went nowhere. After WXYZ contacted Detroit Water and Sewerage Department, Deputy Director Sam Smalley said crews noticed a sewage smell near the lead line work and sent workers out to investigate and fix the issue.

stories.title: DPSCD Continues Long-Term Improvement on 2026 M-STEP Results

The company claims this investment helped restore power to 90% of customers within 48 hours after a recent storm and reduced outage durations by 91% from 2023 to 2025. The proposal, which would allow voters to decide on transitioning to a publicly owned utility system, will remain on the 2026 midterm ballot.

The Dish set out to explore what makes its food scene distinctly 'up north.'

stories.title: Fact check: John James’ link to data center tax breaks, donations

While James did not vote for a $70 billion tax break specific to data centers, he supported the 'Big Beautiful Bill' with broad corporate tax breaks that benefited them. Donors tied to data centers have contributed over $100,000 to his campaigns across multiple election cycles.

stories.title: Fake payroll, millions in loans: Detroit man sentenced in pandemic fraud case
stories.summary: A 46-year-old Detroit man was sentenced to 24 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to a multimillion-dollar pandemic fraud scheme involving false payroll claims and the misuse of relief funds for personal purchases like a Beverly Hills home. The court ordered $2.187 million in restitution and three years of supervised release following his prison term.

photo.alt: A 46-year-old Detroit man was sentenced to 24 months in federal prison after pleading guilty to participating in a multimillion-dollar fraud scheme involving pandemic relief funds.

stories.title: Fall colors are starting in Michigan! How to view foliage across the state
stories.summary: Michigan's fall colors are beginning, with parts of the Upper Peninsula already showing 40-60% leaf change. The article provides an interactive map and suggested viewing locations across the state.

photo.alt: Birch trees in fall.

stories.title: Fall has arrived, does that mean daylight saving time is over?
stories.summary: The start of fall does not coincide with the end of daylight saving time. The autumnal equinox occurred on Sept. 22, but daylight saving time will end later in the season. The article clarifies the distinction between seasonal changes and time adjustments.

photo.alt: Fall daylight saving time

stories.title: Fall is finally here. Does Daylight Saving Time end now?
stories.summary: Michigan is entering fall on September 22, 2026, but Daylight Saving Time ends later on November 1. The article explains the autumnal equinox, meteorological fall dates, and the impact of DST changes on sunrise and sunset times.

stories.title: Family, friends hold vigil for mother killed in random stabbing outside of her job in downtown Detroit
stories.summary: Family and friends gathered to honor Jaquoya Wix, a Detroit woman killed in a random stabbing outside her Chipotle job. The suspect, a man in his 40s, fled the scene, and loved ones remembered her as a loving and resilient person. No charges have been filed against the accused.

photo.alt: Family, friends hold vigil for mother killed in random stabbing outside of her job in downtown Detroit

stories.title: Family Preservation Program Funding Maintained at 2026 Levels
stories.summary: Funding for the MI Family Together program (formerly Families First, Family Reunification, and Families Together Building Solutions) will be maintained at levels not less than those provided as of September 30, 2026.

stories.title: Family remembers Cehic as devoted husband
stories.summary: Cehic, a Bosnian immigrant, worked at a flea market to support his family. His wife, Sanela Grcic, described him as a kind and devoted husband, grieving his loss after her father's death two months prior. He leaves behind his wife, three adult children, and two teenagers.

photo.alt: Family remembers Cehic as devoted husband

stories.title: Family remembers woman killed in random downtown Detroit stabbing
stories.summary: Jaquoya Wix, a 34-year-old woman on break from her Chipotle job in downtown Detroit, was killed in a random stabbing on Sept. 20. Her family shared memories of her positive life changes and expressed grief over her death. Police captured the suspect via surveillance video and confirm the attack was random, with no charges filed yet. The family has started a GoFundMe for funeral expenses and to support her 15-year-old daughter.

photo.alt: Image related to the news story about Jaquoya Wix's stabbing in Detroit

stories.title: Farmington Sidewalk Repairs Could Cost $18M; Committee Awaits Community Survey
stories.summary: A Farmington committee found 11% of town sidewalks in poor condition, estimating repairs to meet current standards could cost $18 million. The committee, which reviewed existing ordinances and surrounding municipalities' practices, will await community survey results before making recommendations on potential town-funded sidewalk repairs and policy changes.

photo.alt: Farmington Sidewalk Repairs Could Cost $18M; Committee Awaits Community Survey

stories.title: 'Fast' meteor shower is set to start. When Orionids will peak
stories.summary: The Orionids meteor shower is set to begin this week and will peak in October, providing an extra bit of flare to the night sky around Halloween. The 'fast' meteor shower typically features 10 to 20 meteors per hour, streaking through the night sky at 41 miles per second, according to NASA. The shower is expected to peak overnight Oct. 21-22 and will be active until Nov. 7.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jenna Prestininzi

stories.title: Faygo smoked wings
stories.summary: Smith & Co., a newly-opened restaurant in Detroit’s midtown, has introduced Red Pop-flavored smoked wings as a menu item. The restaurant, located in a former welding shop, focuses on locally-sourced ingredients from across the state. The dish, listed as a 'small plate' on the menu, costs $13 and includes red pop sweet & sour sauce, marcona almond slaw, and sesame.

photo.alt: Faygo smoked wings

stories.title: FBI Detroit: ‘Uptick’ in child predator arrests, sextortion cases rising among kids, teens
stories.summary: The FBI's Endangered Child Alert Program (ECAP) collaborates with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to identify child predators. FBI Detroit reports a national increase in arrests of alleged predators, with more cases involving online exploitation as children have more digital access. Parents and schools are urged to monitor online activity to prevent exploitation.

photo.alt: FBI Detroit: ‘Uptick’ in child predator arrests, sextortion cases rising among kids, teens

stories.title: Federal appeals court vacates Trump order extending operations for a west Michigan coal plant
stories.summary: A federal appeals court has vacated an order from the Trump administration that extended the operations of the J.H. Campbell Coal Plant in Port Sheldon Township, Michigan. The court ruled that the U.S. Department of Energy exceeded its emergency authority under the Federal Power Act, emphasizing that states, not the federal government, should manage energy reliability planning. The plant, owned by Consumers Energy, was scheduled to close by 2025, with the court's decision aligning with state and regional grid operator approvals for its retirement.

photo.alt: ONN photo/Sarah Leach

stories.title: Federal complaint alleges Medicaid fraud, forced labor by Quality Behavioral Health CEO
stories.summary: The federal government is seeking to seize nearly $19 million from Quality Behavioral Health, alleging its CEO used Medicaid beneficiaries as forced labor and submitted fraudulent claims. The civil forfeiture complaint, filed on September 22, 2026, follows an FBI search of the CEO's home and company locations in August. No criminal charges have been announced against the CEO.

photo.alt: Federal complaint alleges Medicaid fraud, forced labor by Quality Behavioral Health CEO

stories.title: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit over Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts
stories.summary: A federal judge dismissed a lawsuit challenging Title X grant funding for pregnancy prevention efforts, upholding the allocation of these federal health care funds for related programs in Michigan.

stories.title: Federal judge tosses Nessel suit accusing fossil fuel industry of anti-trust violations
stories.summary: A U.S. District Court judge dismissed part of Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel's lawsuit against major fossil fuel companies and the American Petroleum Institute, ruling she lacks standing for federal anti-trust claims. The suit alleged the companies conspired to limit renewable energy competition, but the judge found no proximate cause linking this to higher energy costs for residents. Nessel's office is reviewing the decision and considering next steps.

photo.alt: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel at a press conference with other state attorneys general and governors.

stories.title: Feds defend ICE officers in immigrant’s fatal Michigan car crash
stories.summary: Federal immigration officers were a half-mile away when a man illegally in the U.S. crashed a car at high speed and died in Michigan. The Department of Homeland Security denied officers were pursuing the vehicle when the crash occurred, stating they discontinued the enforcement action for public safety. The incident has sparked anger among activists and prompted an investigation by Michigan state police.

stories.title: Feds sue Michigan company over sexual harassment complaints
stories.summary: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission has sued Davis Cartage Co., a Corunna, Michigan-based transportation company, over allegations that its logistics president, Timothy Ryan, sexually harassed female employees. The lawsuit claims Ryan made unwelcome advances, created a hostile work environment, and was protected by the company’s HR department. Davis Cartage has not yet responded to the complaint.

stories.title: FEMA Imposes Election Administration Conditions on Homeland Security Grants
stories.summary: In June 2026, FEMA issued a Notice of Funding Opportunity requiring states to implement changes to election systems as a condition for Homeland Security Grant Program funds. Requirements include transitioning from electronic voting systems using bar codes/QR codes to hand-marked paper ballots, conducting 5% post-election manual audits, and reconciling voter counts with ballots cast. States must allocate at least 80% of funds to local and tribal governments.

stories.title: Festival of Oddities to move. Organizer says Charlotte is unwelcoming
stories.summary: The organizer of the Festival of Oddities has announced the event will no longer take place in Charlotte due to harassment by a local religious group and inadequate support from city officials. Jenn Carpenter, a festival founder, cited safety concerns and a lack of police response during protests by a church group. The festival, held annually since 2019, plans to relocate to another Mid-Michigan community in 2027.

stories.title: Fewer Michigan students were chronically absent from school in 2025-26
stories.summary: Michigan school districts have implemented creative strategies like student incentives, parent outreach, and home visits to combat chronic absenteeism. Detroit Public Schools Community District saw its chronic absenteeism rate drop to 60% in 2025-26, down from 76.7% in 2021-22. Initiatives include attendance agents, health hubs, free bus rides for students, and competitive programs between districts.

stories.title: Freaks and Geeks
stories.summary: Forever remembered as one of the great non-starters of ’90s television, creator Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow’s sublime “Freaks and Geeks” now exists as one of the most effortlessly perfect things ever created. Set in a fictional Detroit suburb in the year 1980, the show stars Lindsay Weir (Linda Cardellini) and her younger brother Sam (John Francis Daley) as they navigate the awkwardness of high school. Lindsay hangs out with freaks and burnouts: there’s Nick (Jason Segel), the Rush-obsessed aspiring drummer, and Kim (Busy Philipps), the mean girl from a bad part of town. Meanwhile, Sam is an awkward geek who spends most of his time with fellow nerds Neal (Samm Levine) and Bill (Martin Starr). It’s hard to imagine why the show was ever cancelled: Every episode is a treasure trove of [pitch-perfect comedy](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dB_D_ZxGUWA) and [surprisingly tender moments](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cmCpmEQD0L4), featuring nearly every important comedy actor of the aughts and 2010s (no, [really](https://www.looper.com/820224/famous-actors-you-forgot-showed-up-on-freaks-and-geeks/)). Watch it now for an inviting fall atmosphere, a sneaky University of Michigan reference (“I mean, are the kids in Michigan schools that stupid?” might be the best line in the show) and one of the greatest finales in TV history.

stories.title: FY27 General Omnibus Bill Allocates $4.068M for Michigan Veterans and Military Programs

The total state spending for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, is $108,812,200.

stories.title: FY27 General Omnibus Bill Includes 2026 Supplemental Funding and Workforce, Procurement Directives
stories.summary: Michigan's FY27 General Omnibus Bill (SB 878/PA 21 of 2026) includes supplemental funding and mandates annual reports on work project accounts, prioritizes Michigan and veteran-owned businesses for procurement, enforces in-person workforce policies, requires space utilization assessments by July 1, 2027, and outlines federal policy impact reporting deadlines for 2026 and 2027.

stories.title: FY27 General Omnibus Budget Allocates $120.78 Million in State Spending
stories.summary: Michigan's FY27 General Omnibus Budget allocates $120.78 million in total state spending for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, with $10.4 million designated for local government programs. The Department of Agriculture and Rural Development receives $10.4 million for initiatives including agriculture preservation easements, environmental stewardship, and local conservation districts.

stories.title: FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill Includes 2026 Supplemental Funding
stories.summary: The FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill for Michigan includes $200,000 in federal contingency funds and $1 million in state restricted contingency funds, with estimated pension-related legacy costs of $5,008,800 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027. The bill mandates space utilization assessments by agencies by July 1, 2027, and prioritizes in-person work and Michigan-made goods/services in state expenditures.

stories.title: Gilmore Girls
stories.summary: There is no show as synonymous with fall as “Gilmore Girls.” Though the series concluded nearly two decades ago, fans annually rewatch all 153 episodes when summer ends. Following its resurgence with Generation Z, the Lorelais (mother-daughter co-protagonists who share the same name) returned for a renewal miniseries, “Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life,” in 2016, but nothing holds up quite like the original. From Chilton Preparatory School to Yale University, follow Rory Gilmore’s (Alexis Bledel) journey through high school romance, friendship and rivalry, college applications and university life. While she’s funny, relatable and occasionally frustrating, the best part of Rory Gilmore is her heartwarming relationship with her mother, Lorelai (Lauren Graham), as she navigates growing up and finding independence. However, what truly keeps viewers coming back is the cozy, comforting atmosphere the show creates. Set in the small fictional town of Stars Hollow, Conn., the knit sweaters, pumpkin patches, cider mills and close-knit community perfectly embody the warmth of autumn. If you start the show today, you’ll watch the leaves turn and fall alongside the Gilmore girls, ready to do it all over again next year.

photo.alt: A collage of TV characters featuring Abed and Britta from Community, The Gilmore Girls, and Freaks and Geeks.

stories.title: Glacier Detachment in Nepal Triggers Floods in China and Nepal

The event, which mobilized material from a glacier at 5200 m a.s.l., met with previous flood deposits, leading to a dam failure and subsequent flooding. Satellite imagery and photos confirm the detachment and its effects.

Claiming these fraudulent credits can result in civil and criminal penalties. The IRS emphasizes that no such government agreements with tribal groups exist and urges taxpayers to report suspicious offers.

stories.title: Kamala Harris, Abdul El-Sayed focus on Black maternal health at Detroit event
stories.summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris and Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed highlighted Black maternal health disparities during a Detroit event, emphasizing Medicaid cuts and healthcare access challenges. Harris endorsed El-Sayed's campaign, while his Republican opponent Mike Rogers criticized the Democratic agenda. The discussion occurred amid a tight Senate race in Michigan.

stories.summary: Kroger donated $10,000 to Jewish Family Services of Washtenaw County's Nourish Nutrition Services program, which provides meals and food assistance to residents facing food insecurity. The funding supports the program's Shalom Kitchen and Nourish Pantry, which serves nearly 17,000 individuals annually. stories.title: Labor Day Weekend: How Did Students Spend Their Break?
stories.summary: Students in the Ann Arbor school district used the Labor Day break for trips, festivals, work, and family gatherings. While some, like Ellie Ledbetter, traveled to New York City for college tours, others like Lila Sarnecki attended the Detroit Jazz Festival or worked, such as Wesley Saidak’s family celebration at a trailer park. Opinions on the break’s timing varied, with some appreciating the gradual return to school and others finding it disruptive.

source.name: Autumn George, Zoe Hillebrand, Ingrid Kryscynski, and Cam McBurrows
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

stories.title: Labor Day Weekend: How Did Students Spend Their Break?
stories.summary: CHS students shared how they spent their Labor Day weekend break, which included college visits in New York City, attending the Detroit Jazz Festival, and family gatherings at a trailer park. The four-day break (Sept. 4-7) allowed students to ease back into the school year after a short first week. While opinions varied on the break's timing, all students used the time to its fullest potential.

source.name: Autumn George, Zoe Hillebrand, Ingrid Kryscynski, and Cam McBurrows
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

photo.alt: Ellie Ledbetter stands in front of Times Square on her trip to New York City over break. stories.title: Lake Orion village disincorporation petition stalls amid legal dispute
stories.summary: A citizen-led effort to dissolve Lake Orion village has stalled after county officials declined to place the disincorporation question on the ballot, leading to a lawsuit and appeal. The dispute centers on tax rates and governance, with residents arguing that maintaining the village creates duplicate services and higher taxes. A judge dismissed the initial lawsuit, but the case remains unresolved as the county election commission cannot consider the petition due to legal challenges.

stories.title: Lawrence M. Seiford to Retire from University of Michigan

He joined U-M in 2000 and served as department chair and co-director of the Tauber Institute. His research in operations research and data envelopment analysis earned him numerous awards and fellowships.

stories.title: Lee Chatfield embezzlement trial delayed over expert witness dispute
stories.summary: An Ingham County judge delayed the corruption trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield, who faces 13 felony charges for allegedly misusing funds from a political nonprofit and campaign committees. The delay allows Chatfield's attorney to appeal a decision permitting testimony from a state-aligned forensic accountant. Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel criticized the delay as 'outrageous,' while defense attorney Mary Chartier accused the state of poor scheduling and 'disrespect' toward the courts.

photo.alt: Lee Chatfield testifying in court (U.P. Politico / Wikimedia Commons)

stories.title: Lee Chatfield embezzlement trial delayed over expert witness dispute
stories.summary: An Ingham County judge delayed the corruption trial of former Michigan House Speaker Lee Chatfield to allow his attorney to appeal a decision permitting testimony from a state-aligned forensic accountant. The defense argues the witness' expertise is irrelevant to the case, while Attorney General Dana Nessel accused the courts of stalling. The appeals process could extend beyond Nessel's tenure in office.

photo.alt: An Ingham County judge put the corruption trial of a former Michigan House speaker on hold Monday.

stories.title: Lee Chatfield trial delayed again, this time over disputed expert witness
stories.summary: Lee Chatfield’s trial was delayed again after his attorney appealed a judge’s decision to allow a forensic accountant as an expert witness. The appeal could push the trial into 2027, after Attorney General Dana Nessel leaves office, and centers on disputed financial reports. Chatfield faces 13 felony counts related to alleged embezzlement from 2020-2021, including funding personal expenses through political fundraising accounts.

photo.alt: Lee Chatfield trial delay over disputed expert witness

stories.title: Legislative Directed Spending Reporting Mandated
stories.summary: The Michigan legislature must submit a jointly agreed-upon list of legislatively directed spending items to the state budget office within 30 days of enactment. Agencies must publicly report grant details by March 15, June 15, and September 15 of the fiscal year.

stories.title: Legislatively Directed Spending Items Must Be Publicly Disclosed
stories.summary: The legislature must submit a list of legislatively directed spending items to the state budget office within 30 days of the act's effective date. Departments must also post and update reports on these items by March 15, June 15, and September 15 each fiscal year.

stories.title: Legislature Intends to Fund Native American Tuition Waivers for Public Universities
stories.summary: For the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, the Michigan legislature intends to allocate funds for unfunded North American Indian tuition waiver costs at public universities. A report on these waivers, including application numbers and student enrollment data, must be submitted by January 15 of each year.

stories.title: Lessons from Detroit’s ShotStoppers Community Violence Intervention Program
stories.summary: The City of Detroit’s ShotStoppers program, launched in 2023, funds community-based organizations to reduce gun violence through targeted interventions and community engagement. Evaluations show decreases in homicides and non-fatal shootings in designated zones, with teams using strategies like individual outreach and resource provision. Trust and credibility with at-risk individuals and communities were critical to success, supported by the city’s financial backing and operational autonomy.

source.name: Sam Stragand
source.publication: Poverty Solutions at the University of Michigan

stories.title: Local leaders agree: data center regulations are needed
stories.summary: Local government leaders across Michigan support state regulations for data centers, according to a survey by the University of Michigan’s Center for Local, State and Urban Policy. Nearly 60% of respondents believe setting rules should be a high priority for lawmakers, while 55% anticipate strong opposition to data centers. Rural communities show higher opposition, with 53% of local politicians stating data centers’ costs outweigh their benefits. Concerns include decommissioning plans, health and environmental impacts, and water use.

photo.alt: Community violence intervention initiative image

stories.title: LSA announces pilot program making first-semester grades pass/fail, beginning 2027
stories.summary: The University of Michigan’s College of Literature, Science and the Arts announced a pilot program on Aug. 5 that will make first-semester grades for first-year LSA students pass/fail starting in fall 2027. While students will still receive assignment grades and instructor feedback, final grades will not appear on external transcripts or GPAs. The program aims to reduce academic pressure and encourage exploration of new subjects without long-term grade consequences.

photo.alt: Students sit in front of a wall of windows in the LSA building.

stories.title: LSA announces pilot program making first-semester grades pass/fail, beginning 2027
stories.summary: The University of Michigan’s College of Literature, Science and the Arts announced a pilot program starting fall 2027 that will designate first-semester grades for first-year LSA students as Pass or No Credit on transcripts. Students will still receive assignment grades and feedback, but these will not affect GPAs. The program aims to help students acclimate to college demands and explore academic interests without grade-related pressure.

photo.alt: Students sit in front of a wall of windows in the LSA building.

stories.title: LSA pauses first-semester pass/no credit grading pilot program
stories.summary: LSA announced a pause to its first-semester pass/no credit grading pilot program, initially scheduled for fall 2027, following a request from University leadership for further analysis. The program aimed to help first-year students transition to campus and address mental health concerns but faced criticism over academic rigor and grade inflation.

photo.alt: LSA Building at the University of Michigan

stories.title: LSA pauses first-semester pass/no credit grading pilot program
stories.summary: The College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) has paused its first-semester pass/no credit grading pilot program, which was set to begin in fall 2027. University leadership requested the pause to allow for further input, analysis, and discussion. The program aimed to let first-year students receive grades and feedback without GPA impacts, but faced criticism over academic rigor and grade inflation while supporters argued it would reduce pressure on students.

photo.alt: The LSA Building on a clear day. A sign in the front reads, “Literature, Science, and the Arts Building.”

stories.title: Lucy Kaplansky
stories.summary: Lucy Kaplansky is an acclaimed singer-songwriter with nine critically acclaimed CDs, including two Best Pop Album awards from the Association for Independent Music. Her 2012 album 'Reunion' was praised by National Public Radio as 'a master class in making the personal universal.'

stories.title: Macomb County eyes $6.79M cloud platform for emergency records, dispatch
stories.summary: Macomb County will migrate its emergency dispatch and records management systems to a cloud-based platform under a $6.79 million contract with Tyler Technologies. The Records and Public Safety Committee approved the five-year agreement on Sept. 17, 2026, which consolidates public safety technology across municipal boundaries and aims to enhance data sharing between agencies. The Sheriff’s Office will pay $2.1 million over five years, with affiliated agencies covering the remaining $4.7 million.

photo.alt: Residents speak during public comment at the Macomb County Board of Commissioners meeting.

stories.title: Madison Heights woman accused of trafficking victim brought her child along, prosecutors say
stories.summary: A Madison Heights woman faces human trafficking charges after a months-long investigation. Maya Scott Perry was arrested on June 17 for allegedly trafficking a woman for prostitution and bringing her minor child during activities, though the child was not harmed. She is charged with five felonies and one misdemeanor, with a $250,000 bond.

photo.alt: Maya Scott Perry (Courtesy of Madison Heights Police Department)

stories.title: Major rural road reopen with new roundabout west of Ann Arbor
stories.summary: A new single-lane roundabout at the intersection of Scio Church and Zeeb roads west of Ann Arbor has reopened after a three-month closure. The project was delayed in late August when a motorist damaged the construction site by bypassing safety barricades and driving over freshly poured concrete. The roundabout aims to address traffic congestion and reduce angle crashes at the intersection.

photo.alt: A new single-lane roundabout is complete and open to traffic at Zeeb and Scio Church roads, as shown in the Washtenaw County Road Commission's announcement.Provided by Washtenaw County Road Commission

stories.title: Man accused of killing woman in random attack in downtown Detroit denied bond
stories.summary: Devon Jason Watson was charged with first-degree murder for stabbing Jaquoya Wix, 34, to death in a random attack in downtown Detroit on Sept. 20. Watson was arraigned via Zoom on Sept. 23 and denied bond. The Wayne County Prosecutor’s Office stated the attack was random, and Watson has prior assault convictions.

photo.alt: Devon Watson appears for his arraignment via Zoom on Sept. 23, 2026. (WDIV)

stories.title: Man arrested after police seize hundreds of pills, multiple weapons from Shelby Township home
stories.summary: A search warrant at a Shelby Township home led to the seizure of hundreds of oxycodone and amphetamine pills, multiple weapons, and the arrest of 45-year-old Mark Cholagh. Detectives from the Macomb County Sheriff’s Office and Warren Police Department executed the warrant on Sept. 17, recovering firearms, ammunition, drug paraphernalia, and $16,000 in cash. Cholagh faces felony charges related to drug distribution and firearm offenses.

photo.alt: Mark Cholagh, 45, of Macomb Township, is facing multiple charges after a police search warrant in Shelby Township uncovered multiple guns, hundreds of pills, drug paraphernalia, packaging materials and cash.

stories.title: Man charged with felonies for driving intoxicated after 3 passengers seriously injured in crash
stories.summary: A man has been charged with two felonies related to operating while intoxicated and seriously injuring three passengers in a crash on Saturday in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. Donevan Brueggeman, 27, of Cedarville, faces charges of operating under the influence causing incapacitating injury and a moving violation causing serious impairment of body function. He was arraigned on September 29, 2026, with a $10,000 bond.

stories.title: Man dead after fleeing ICE agents in Grand Rapids
stories.summary: A man is dead after crashing his car while fleeing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in Grand Rapids on Sept. 20, 2026. The crash occurred near Century Avenue and McKendrick Street, with the driver pronounced dead at the scene. ICE agents attempted to stop him before the crash, and the Grand Rapids Police Department has referred the investigation to Michigan State Police due to the case's complexity. U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten has demanded transparency and accountability from ICE regarding the incident.

stories.title: Man found dead in Genesee Township driveway after shooting
stories.summary: A 60-year-old man was found dead on Sunday morning in a driveway in Genesee Township after a shooting. Police were dispatched to the 3000 block of Drexel Avenue at 5:15 a.m. on Sept. 20 and are actively investigating. The incident appears to be isolated, with suspects identified, and the Michigan State Police Crime Lab is assisting.

The event, hosted at Jenison High School in Georgetown Twp., MI, featured multiple flights with bands from various schools competing in music, visual, and general effect categories.

stories.title: Marching bands: Vote for MLive's Band of the Week in West Michigan
stories.summary: MLive has launched a weekly poll for readers to select their favorite high school marching band in West and Southwest Michigan. The first competition of the season occurred on Sept. 19, 2026 at Jenison High School, with the winning band receiving a special story each week. The poll opens Monday morning and closes at noon Tuesday, with results announced later in the week.

stories.title: Marching bands: West Michigan kicks off competition season at Jenison Invitational

Twelve bands performed themes ranging from the New Orleans bayou to outer space, with judges awarding top performers across five flights and caption awards for music, props, and costumes.

stories.title: Margaret (Peggy) L. Carver Retires as Associate Professor of Pharmacy
stories.summary: Margaret Carver, a global leader in infectious diseases and bioinorganic chemistry, retires on August 30, 2026. She was the first female president of the Society of Infectious Diseases Pharmacists and contributed to over 60 publications. Carver also served on the College of Pharmacy admissions committee for 29 years.

source.name: University of Michigan Museum of Natural History

stories.title: Margaret (Peggy) L. Carver Retires from University of Michigan
stories.summary: Margaret (Peggy) L. Carver, associate professor of pharmacy, retires on August 30, 2026. A global leader in infectious diseases and bioinorganic chemistry, she contributed to over 60 publications and 12 editions of the DiPiro Pharmacotherapy text. She received the COP Teaching Excellence Award twice and mentored for 40 years.

stories.title: Marines’ hostile-fire pay doubles to $450 a month after 23-year freeze

stories.title: Maritime and Port Facilities Assistance Program Appropriation
stories.summary: The Michigan budget document outlines a $2,800 one-time appropriation for maritime and port facilities assistance grants under 2022 PA 159, prioritizing projects aligned with specific allowable uses in the legislation.

stories.title: Market Support
stories.summary: Grandmont Rosedale Development Corp.’s Northwest Detroit Farmers’ Market is hiring someone to assist with set-up and breakdown every Thursday through Oct. 8. The position pays $100 each market day. Email educkett@grandmontrosedale.com to apply.

stories.title: Marshall woman arrested for suspected drunken driving after crashing twice
stories.summary: A 50-year-old Marshall woman was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence after striking a parked vehicle and fleeing the scene on Sept. 21. Chelsea police officers later stopped her vehicle, where an open vodka bottle was found, and she exhibited signs of intoxication. The case remains open pending lab analysis and potential charges.

photo.alt: MLive file photo.

stories.title: Mason Projects Plan Pre-K Expansion and HVAC Upgrades
stories.summary: The Mason projects, involving Pre-K classroom expansion, heating/cooling, and doors/windows upgrades, are in the Pre-Planning stage with a $6.09 million investment. Completion is expected by Fall 2029, though the start date remains TBD.

stories.title: Massive Plastics Factory Fire in South Haven Under Investigation; No Injuries Reported
stories.summary: A massive fire at East Jordan Plastics in South Haven is under investigation, with no injuries reported. The fire, which started near a propane filling station, required 17 fire departments and extensive water to extinguish. Cleanup continues as the company prepares to reopen later this week.

photo.alt: East Jordan Plastics in South Haven after a fire on Sept. 28, 2026

stories.title: MDHHS Fails to Report Required MPHI Project Information to Legislature
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Health and Human Services (MDHHS) did not report all required information for MPHI projects funded by state appropriations, leading to potential noncompliance and reduced transparency. An audit found that 10% of 20 agreements totaling $10.6 million had no reported project information, while 28% of 18 agreements lacked detailed descriptions and funding details. The audit also noted missing subgrantee information for two agreements.

source.name: Michigan Advance
source.publication: Michigan Office of the Auditor General

stories.title: MDHHS warns about health risks of recreational nitrous oxide use
stories.summary: Michigan’s health department issued a warning about the dangers of recreational nitrous oxide use, linking it to anxiety, memory problems, anemia, and loss of consciousness. Data shows a rise in emergency cases, with 34% requiring hospitalization in 2024. The department urges immediate medical attention for affected individuals.

photo.alt: MDHHS warns about health risks of recreational nitrous oxide use

stories.summary: Learn about the candidates running for Michigan's 6th District in the United States House of Representatives.

stories.summary: Schoolcraft College men's hockey captains were highlighted as the team prepares for the season. The article features an image of the captains and discusses their leadership roles.

photo.alt: The Hunt Begins

stories.title: Mexican American Council’s ARPA funding compliance addressed by city leaders
stories.summary: Saginaw City Manager Tim Morales said an organization that received $620,000 in city-provided federal funds remains under compliance despite questions about the group’s eligibility. The Saginaw City Council approved multiple rounds of federal American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funding for the Mexican American Council, including $500,000 in January 2023 and an additional $120,000 the following year. At the council’s Monday, Sept. 14 meeting, council members asked Morales for an update on the Mexican American Council’s status as an eligible recipient of the money. Media reports last week questioned the organization’s eligibility to receive ARPA funds as well as its status as a nonprofit.

photo.alt: Mexican American Council’s ARPA funding compliance addressed by city leaders

stories.summary: Michael N. Bastedo has been appointed as senior associate dean at the Marsal Family School of Education for a term from Sept. 1, 2026, through June 30, 2028.

stories.title: Michael Siegrist Recognized as Township Clerk of the Year
stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft College alumnus, was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year for his dedication to election integrity. He emphasizes the importance of a secure democratic process and encourages community involvement in elections.

photo.alt: Michael Siegrist

stories.title: Michigan absentee ballots are going out. How to get yours, track it
stories.summary: Michigan officials began sending out absentee ballots for the November general election on Sept. 24, 2026. Voters can still request and fill out ballots online or in person at local clerk's offices. Absentee ballots are sent out 40 days before Election Day in Michigan.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: Michigan Adopts USDA Guidelines for WIC Program Eligibility
stories.summary: The state will use USDA-established income eligibility and verification guidelines to determine WIC program eligibility, aligning with current WIC policy.

stories.title: Michigan AG candidate Doug Lloyd cut charges, sought no jail in sex-crime cases
stories.summary: Republican Doug Lloyd is running for Michigan attorney general on his three decades of experience as a prosecutor. However, a Metro Times review of court records and case files found instances during his tenure as Eaton County prosecutor where cases involving sexual assault, child exploitation, and domestic violence resulted in reduced charges, probation instead of jail, or no prosecution. The findings emerge as Lloyd faces Democrat Eli Savit in a closely contested race to succeed term-limited Attorney General Dana Nessel.

photo.alt: Doug Lloyd, Michigan AG candidate

stories.summary: A Metro Times review found multiple cases in which defendants accused of sexual misconduct avoided incarceration.
