stories.title: Michigan Agencies to Post Grant Reports by March 15 and Update by June 15 and September 15
stories.summary: Michigan state agencies must post grant reports by March 15 of the fiscal year and update them by June 15 and September 15. The reports must include comprehensive information about grants awarded, as mandated by the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.3 Million for Stormwater Management in Ox Creek Watershed
stories.summary: The state has allocated $1.3 million for a stormwater management project in the Ox Creek Watershed. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.595 Billion for Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity in FY2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Opportunity will receive $1.595 billion in funding for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, including $355.5 million from the state general fund and over $1 billion in federal revenues.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1.5M for Pediatric Dentistry Clinic
stories.summary: The Department of Health will allocate $1.5 million to Team Cares to support a pediatric and sedation dentistry clinic. The project, funded through work project funds, will be completed by September 30, 2030, and is managed by a CARF International accredited wellness center.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1 Million for Future Mobility and Electrification Projects
stories.summary: The state of Michigan has allocated $1 million to support the emerging aviation and advanced air mobility sector through the Office of Future Mobility and Electrification. Funds will be used for infrastructure deployment, industry development, and workforce strategies. The project is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1 Million for Literacy Program Implementation
stories.summary: The state appropriates at least $1 million for implementation costs of literacy programs funded under the state school aid act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $125,000 for Renewable Energy and Electrification Infrastructure Grants
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission will review and award grants for renewable energy and electrification infrastructure projects, prioritizing distressed areas defined by blight designations, high poverty/unemployment rates, or environmental burdens. Recipients must submit post-project reports and administrative costs are capped at $125,000. RNG is defined as methane from organic waste sources.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $13.9 Million for Higher Education and Student Support in 2026-2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 includes $13.9 million in appropriations for the Office of Higher Education, covering dual enrollment payments, student financial assistance programs, and classified positions. An additional $4 million in one-time funding supports college success initiatives, wraparound student services, and adult education programs. Funds are sourced from the state general fund, merit award trust fund, and other restricted revenues.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $150,000 for School Board Member Training
stories.summary: The state allocates $150,000 for school board member training programs covering topics like conflicts of interest, labor relations, education law, and governance.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $150M for Educator Compensation in 2026-2027
stories.summary: The Michigan legislature allocates $150 million for 2026-2027 to increase educator compensation in districts and intermediate districts. Funds must be used for educator pay raises, with collective bargaining required if unions are present. Payments are defined as 1-time bonuses not counted toward retirement contributions.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $174M for Pension Legacy Costs in FY27 Budget
stories.summary: The FY27 General Omnibus Bill (SB 878/PA 21 of 2026) authorizes $174.4 million in pension-related legacy costs for Michigan state departments through September 30, 2027. The budget includes administrative requirements for fund expenditure, reporting obligations for work project accounts, and policies prioritizing American and Michigan-made goods and services. Additional provisions address workforce management, space utilization assessments, and support for geographically disadvantaged businesses.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $18 Million for Workforce Development Projects
stories.summary: The state has designated $18 million for workforce development to meet federal work requirements under Public Law 119-21. Unexpended funds will remain available until projects are completed, with a tentative completion date of September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $190,000 for Educator Recruitment and Preparation Programs
stories.summary: The state budget allocates at least $190,000 and 1.0 FTE position for educator recruitment and preparation programs from funds appropriated in part 1.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $1M for Group-Based Prenatal Care Programs
stories.summary: The state will allocate $1 million to support prenatal healthcare providers offering group-based prenatal care programs. These programs involve small groups of expectant mothers in the same pregnancy phase receiving health services and discussions.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2.75M for Rural Home Visit Program
stories.summary: The state will allocate at least $2.75 million from the general fund to support a rural home visit program for prenatal care. The Department of Health and Human Services must give equal consideration to all eligible evidence-based providers across regions when contracting for these services.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2.9M for Northwest Michigan Dental Clinic Expansion
stories.summary: The Department of Health will allocate $2.9 million to Northwest Michigan Health Services, Inc., to open a larger, more comprehensive dental clinic supporting United We Smile. The project aims to improve dental care access in the region.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2 Million for SMART Manufacturing Grant Program
stories.summary: The state has allocated $2 million for a SMART manufacturing grant program. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $2 Million for Tribal Government Grants
stories.summary: Michigan has appropriated $2 million for tribal government grants to fund essential services for federally recognized tribal governments. Funds will be distributed according to an allocation plan recommended by the Inter-Tribal Council of Michigan.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $200K for Volunteer Dental Program for the Uninsured
stories.summary: A competitive grant of $200,000 will be allocated to administer a volunteer dental program providing services to uninsured individuals. The funding comes from dental program appropriations.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $20M for Community Navigation Partners
stories.summary: The state will allocate up to $20 million to community navigation partners to assist Michiganders in maintaining healthcare access during Medicaid and SNAP eligibility changes. The program prioritizes MI Bridges Community Partners and provides outreach and support through nonprofit agencies.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $23.5M for Direct Care Wage Increase in 2027
stories.summary: The state has allocated $23.5 million to continue direct care wage increases effective January 1, 2027, under the Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act. Funds will support minimum hourly wage rate increases.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $250,000 for AI Model Policies and Integration
stories.summary: A one-time appropriation of $250,000 will fund the development of state AI policies and tools for education. The funds will support integrating artificial intelligence into teaching, learning, and assessment services for school districts.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $250,000 to Veterans' Apprenticeship Programs in Construction Industry
stories.summary: The state of Michigan has allocated $250,000 to recruit and assist veterans in transitioning into apprenticeship programs within the construction industry. These funds may be contracted to a national nonprofit program that connects military service members with skilled training opportunities.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $299,700 for Maternal Health Policy Implementation
stories.summary: The state will allocate $299,700 to implement 2024 PA 256, which covers maternal health policy changes under Michigan Compiled Law 395.361 to 395.369. This funding supports legislative mandates for maternal health improvements.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $310 Million for School Safety and Mental Health in 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 Budgets
stories.summary: Michigan has allocated $300 million from the state school aid fund and $21 million from the general fund for the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 fiscal years to support school safety and mental health initiatives. Funds may be used to hire or contract support staff for student mental health needs, including school psychologists, and to provide payments to districts, intermediate districts, nonpublic schools, and the Michigan Schools for the Deaf and Blind that opt in. The estimated completion date of the work project is December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4.26M for Dental Oral Assessment Program
stories.summary: The state will allocate $4.26 million, plus private contributions, to establish and maintain a dental oral assessment program. A report summarizing dental reports from schools must be submitted by December 31 of the current fiscal year.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4.406 Million for Heavy-Duty Vehicles Program
stories.summary: The state has allocated $4.406 million for a heavy-duty vehicles program. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4M for Home Help Caregiver Council
stories.summary: Funds are designated to support the Home Help Caregiver Council and related activities under the 2024 PA 144 act, with an estimated cost of $4,000,000.00 by September 30, 2031.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $4M for Prenatal Care Outreach
stories.summary: The state will allocate $4,000,000.00 for prenatal care outreach and service delivery support, following the same allocation method as described in section 1348 of the budget act.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5.6M for Robotics Education Grants in 2025-2026 Budget
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature has allocated $5.6 million for competitive grants to support robotics education programs in public and nonpublic schools. Funds will support pre-K to 12th grade students through partnerships with providers like FIRST Robotics and VEX. Payments must be made by December 1, 2026, with continued funding intended through 2027-2028.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5M for Local Collaboratives to Improve Maternal and Infant Health
stories.summary: The state will allocate $5 million to support grants for local collaboratives that coordinate maternal and infant health outcomes. Recipients must be part of a perinatal quality collaborative.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $5M for Mobile Health Alliance Community Screenings
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Health will allocate $5 million to Mobile Health Alliance for community health screenings and data collection on underserved populations, first responders, and veterans. The project, funded through work project funds, aims to reduce health disparities in rural and medically underserved communities by 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $6.5 Million for Detroit and Rouge River Restoration
stories.summary: The state has allocated $6.5 million for restoration work in the Detroit and Rouge River areas of concern. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $685,000 for High-Emission Vehicle Replacement
stories.summary: The state has allocated $685,000 to replace high-emission vehicles. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates $700,000 for Food Waste Reduction Initiative
stories.summary: The state has allocated $700,000 to support food waste reduction efforts. The project will be executed by state employees or contracted service providers and is expected to be completed by September 30, 2030.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Early Childhood Education and Literacy Programs
stories.summary: The Michigan Legislature has allocated funds for early childhood education and literacy programs, aiming to increase workforce numbers, enhance professional development, and support literacy coaches in intermediate districts. The initiatives include stipends, grants, and partnerships with public universities, with a completion date set for September 30, 2029.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Educator Development and Grow Your Own Programs
stories.summary: Michigan has allocated $70 million for 2025-2026 and $25 million for 2026-2027 to support educator development and 'grow your own' programs through competitive grants. Funds will be distributed to districts, intermediate districts, and consortia for teacher recruitment, retention, and training, with requirements for cost-free participation and partnerships with accredited educator preparation programs. Programs must address critical education workforce needs and demonstrate measurable outcomes.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Funds for Special Education Programs in 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 Fiscal Years
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature has allocated state and federal funds for special education programs in the 2025-2026 and 2026-2027 fiscal years, including reimbursements for districts and intermediate districts. The document outlines specific funding amounts, a weighted funding formula intent for 2028, and provisions for remote learning research and assessment tools development.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Rural Jobs and Capital Investment Funds
stories.summary: Funds from the rural jobs and capital investment appropriation will be used to provide grants, loans, or other economic assistance to rural areas in Michigan through the MEDC and state departments. Unexpended funds will remain available until projects are completed.

stories.title: Michigan Allocates Supplemental Funding for 2026 with Contingency Authorizations and Legacy Cost Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2027 includes $26.4 million in contingency authorizations across federal, state, local, and private sectors, along with $21.5 million in pension-related legacy costs. The document outlines reporting requirements for work project funds, in-person workforce utilization, and restrictions on foreign goods procurement. Funds are subject to transfer rules under the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Allows ARPA Fund Reallocation for Public Health and Safety Employee Payroll
stories.summary: The state budget director may reallocate ARPA funds to reclassify general fund appropriations for payroll and benefits of eligible public health and safety employees at the Department of Corrections and State Police. Reallocation must comply with ARPA guidance and notify legislative committees within 10 business days.

stories.title: Michigan Allows Carryover of Unexpended Teacher Testing Fees
stories.summary: Revenue from unexpended teacher testing fees at the end of the fiscal year may be carried over to the next year and will not revert to the general fund.

stories.title: Michigan and 21 other states win suit against Trump's USDA
stories.summary: Michigan and 21 other states won a federal court case against the Trump administration's USDA, blocking guidelines that restricted SNAP eligibility for non-citizens. The court ruled the USDA's retroactive adjustment period was invalid, preventing potential financial penalties for states. The decision does not reverse eligibility restrictions from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

photo.alt: Michigan residents receiving SNAP benefits

stories.title: Michigan Announces Fiscal Year 2026 Supplemental Budget Allocations
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2025-2026 allocates $45 million in total state spending, with $27.97 million directed to local units of government through acquisition and development grants-in-aid. The document also details lapsing funds for specific natural resources trust projects, including $300,000 for Sycamore Creek Land Acquisition and $1.2 million for Rogue River State Game Area Land Acquisition, which will be reallocated to the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund. Additional provisions include perpetual public recreation land use requirements and mineral royalty agreements for parcels over 5 acres.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates $2.6 Billion for Higher Education in 2027 Fiscal Year
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027, allocates $2.6 billion for higher education. Funding includes federal revenues, state general funds, and other restricted sources, with specific appropriations detailed for public universities like Central Michigan University, Eastern Michigan University, and others. Community colleges must meet performance funding criteria, including participation in the Michigan Transfer Network.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates Funds for Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential
stories.summary: The Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement, and Potential receives line-item appropriations for fiscal year 2026-2027, including 6.0 full-time unclassified positions.

stories.title: Michigan Appropriates Over $8.1 Billion for State Transportation Department in FY2026-2027 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan state transportation department has been allocated over $8.1 billion for the fiscal year 2026-2027, including interdepartmental grants, federal revenues, and other restricted funds. The budget outlines gross appropriation, adjusted gross appropriation, and various revenue sources. The funds are intended for transportation-related projects and services, with no direct allocation from the state general fund.

stories.title: Michigan Attorney General's Legal Reimbursements and Reporting Requirements
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Attorney General must submit a report by March 1 detailing reimbursements received under the State Correctional Facility Reimbursement Act, including expenditure descriptions, investigation costs, and general fund credits. This provision outlines specific reporting obligations for legal reimbursements related to the Michigan Department of Corrections.

stories.title: Michigan Bill Allocates $2.3 Billion for Higher Education in 2026-2027 Fiscal Year
stories.summary: A Michigan legislative bill (HCB 5630) appropriates $2.3 billion for higher education in the 2026-2027 fiscal year, with conditions requiring community colleges to participate in the Michigan Transfer Network and submit course equivalency updates. Performance funding payments are contingent on compliance with these requirements.

stories.title: Michigan Bill Allocates $3M for Literacy Programs via Public Universities
stories.summary: A Michigan legislative bill proposes allocating up to $3 million to a public university partnered with a statewide educational media service. The funds must expand literacy programming, educator resources, and family engagement, with requirements for free standards-aligned content delivery through broadcast and digital platforms. The implementation deadline is February 1, 2028.

stories.title: Michigan Bill Outlines Funding for Teacher Education and Student Support Services
stories.summary: The bill allows approved teacher education institutions to use student support services funding in coordination with Morris Hood, Jr. funding. Institutions must report unobligated funds by April 15, 2026, with unspent funds reallocated to other institutions. The state budget director is required to expend all fiscal recovery funds by December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan bill would shift election duties if the secretary of state also runs for office
stories.summary: A proposed Michigan bill (House Bill 5968) would require the deputy secretary of state to assume election oversight duties when the secretary of state is running for any office other than reelection. The legislation, backed by House Republicans, aims to formalize voluntary recusal policies like those implemented by Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson, who is currently the Democratic gubernatorial nominee. The bill would not apply to election audits or constitutional requirements, and critics argue it targets specific individuals rather than addressing broader election administration issues.

photo.alt: Michigan bill would shift election duties if the secretary of state also runs for office

stories.title: Michigan bills aimed at improving student literacy clear House committee
stories.summary: Three bills aimed at improving student literacy in Michigan have cleared a House committee. The legislation includes requirements for teacher training in reading instruction and support for students with dyslexia. State and national exam results highlight ongoing challenges in literacy proficiency among Michigan students.

photo.alt: Elaine Cromie / Chalkbeat

stories.title: Michigan bird migration season is flying by. Here’s where to see the birds and how to protect them
stories.summary: Thousands of birds migrate through Michigan in late September and early October, with over 380 species passing through. Birdwatchers can spot warblers and other species at locations like the Nichols Arboretum, but birds face hazards like building collisions and climate change impacts.

photo.alt: An illustration of birds migrating at night with a glowing cityscape in the background.

stories.title: Michigan bottle return rate falls to 69.4% as retailers push to overhaul bottle bill
stories.summary: The Midwest Independent Retailers Association surveyed Michigan stores, finding over 90% want bottles and cans removed from grocery stores due to health, safety, and labor concerns. Retailers argue the process is time-consuming, dirty, and offers no financial benefit, prompting calls to reform the bottle bill system.

photo.alt: Image related to the bottle return issue

stories.title: Michigan Budget Allocates Funds for Interstate Licensure Compact Implementation
stories.summary: Funds for compact implementation fees will cover dues, IT systems, and costs for interstate licensure compacts the state joins or is already a member of.

stories.title: Michigan Chamber of Commerce endorses John James for governor
stories.summary: The Michigan Chamber of Commerce endorsed Republican John James for governor of Michigan in the Nov. 3 general election.

photo.alt: Advance-at-a-glance-political-roundup

stories.title: Michigan Chamber of Commerce endorses Mike Rogers for U.S. Senate
stories.summary: The Michigan Chamber of Commerce has endorsed Republican nominee Mike Rogers in his campaign for the U.S. Senate.

photo.alt: Advance-at-a-glance-political-roundup

stories.title: Michigan congresswoman pitches bipartisan bill as way to lower child care costs
stories.summary: Despite the Childcare Modernization Act having Democratic and Republican support, the slow political process in Washington D.C. is keeping it from getting passed.

photo.alt: Kids Club is a complimentary child care service in Flagstaff, Arizona.

stories.title: Michigan country artist Waylon Hanel wins Artist of the Year at Nashville awards show
stories.summary: Waylon Hanel, a self-taught traditional country singer-songwriter from Millington, Michigan, won the Artist of the Year – Traditional/Classic Country award at the 2026 Josie Music Awards on Sunday, Sept. 20, at the Grand Ole Opry House in Nashville.

photo.alt: Michigan country artist Waylon Hanel wins Artist of the Year at Nashville awards show

stories.title: Michigan Court of Appeals directed to review convicted school shooter Ethan Crumbley's appeal of life without parole sentence
stories.summary: A Michigan court has directed a review of Ethan Crumbley's life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. The case involves determining if the teen should be eligible for parole after serving his sentence.

photo.alt: Oakland County Prosecutor Karen McDonald proceeds with an opening statement as defendant Ethan Crumbley listens in Pontiac, Michigan.

stories.title: Michigan dam safety overhaul advances after years of failed attempts
stories.summary: Lawmakers are advancing a sweeping rewrite of Michigan’s dam safety law, six years after a catastrophic failure exposed weaknesses in how aging dams are regulated. The Michigan House voted 96-7 on Sept. 22, 2026, to approve Senate Bill 947, which would require more frequent inspections of high-risk dams, establish a new registration system for dam owners, and mandate long-term maintenance planning. The bipartisan effort follows the 2020 Edenville and Sanford dam failures, which caused $175 million in property damage and forced thousands to evacuate.

photo.alt: LaBarge Dam on the Thornapple River near Caledonia, Mich., March 20, 2026. Federal regulators rated the high-hazard dam in poor condition following a September 2025 inspection.

stories.title: Michigan data-center tax incentives secret
stories.summary: Revisits the 2024 expansion of Michigan’s sales and use tax exemption for data centers, highlighting that the law prevents the Michigan Economic Development Corporation from disclosing information about applicants.

photo.alt: Michigan Data Center Report

stories.title: Michigan Department to Establish Precontract Risk Assessment Policy
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Insurance and Financial Services must establish a policy for conducting precontract risk assessments to evaluate contractor financial risk, security risks, and insurance requirements. A report on assessments and contracts executed under the policy is due by March 31, 2027.

stories.title: Michigan Departments Required to Report Federal Policy Impacts
stories.summary: By December 31 and June 1, Michigan departments must report federal guidelines, rules, or policy changes that significantly impact their operations, including changes in federal revenue and public health or welfare implications.

stories.title: Michigan Designates $10M for Nursing Home Staffing Initiative
stories.summary: Unexpended funds for nursing facility staffing are designated as work project appropriations, aiming to address chronic workforce shortages with an estimated completion cost of $10,000,000.00 by September 30, 2031.

stories.title: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funding for English learners. Here’s what’s at stake.
stories.summary: Michigan districts report insufficient funding for English learners, highlighting ongoing challenges in supporting this student population.

photo.alt: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funding for English learners. Here’s what’s at stake.

stories.title: Michigan districts say they don’t receive enough funds for English learners
stories.summary: Districts in Michigan report insufficient funding for students learning English, particularly those with higher English proficiency. There are no specific funds for students still developing their English comprehension.

photo.alt: Distritos de Michigan dicen que no reciben suficientes fondos para estudiantes que aprenden inglés. Esto es lo que está en riesgo.

stories.title: Michigan DNR rescues lake sturgeon from shallow pool near Ontonagon River
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Natural Resources rescued a lake sturgeon from a shallow pool near the Ontonagon River. Recent research suggests these ancient fish can live up to 300 years, challenging previous estimates.

photo.alt: Michigan DNR rescues lake sturgeon from shallow pool near Ontonagon River

stories.title: Michigan Enhances Prenatal Care Education and Outreach
stories.summary: The state will expand education and outreach efforts to encourage women of childbearing age to seek early pregnancy confirmation and initiate prenatal care. Programs will focus on reducing barriers to care, promoting best practices, and tracking birth outcomes related to substance exposure and preventable diseases.

stories.title: Michigan Expands Fetal Alcohol Syndrome Outreach and Prevention
stories.summary: The state will continue developing outreach programs focused on fetal alcohol syndrome services, including health promotion, prevention, and intervention. The department will also explore federal grants to reduce alcohol and marijuana use among pregnant women.

stories.title: Michigan Forecast: Next weather change just starting to show up. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update
stories.summary: The weather forecast for Michigan highlights continued fall sunshine and warm afternoons through mid-next week, followed by recurring strong cold fronts every three to four days. Residents are encouraged to watch live updates and forecasts on MLive's weather page.

photo.alt: Michigan Forecast: Next weather change just starting to show up. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update

stories.title: Michigan Forecast: Small showers far south, but otherwise fantastic for September. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update
stories.summary: The weather forecast for Michigan predicts small showers in the southern regions, with otherwise pleasant conditions for September. Viewers are encouraged to watch Mark Torregrossa's live weather update for more details.

photo.alt: Michigan Forecast: Small showers far south, but otherwise fantastic for September. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update

stories.title: Michigan Forecast: Suddenly we go bone-dry in weather. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update
stories.summary: Michigan is entering a quiet and enjoyable weather pattern that is expected to last at least a week. The article highlights the upcoming dry weather and encourages viewers to watch the live weather update for more details.

photo.alt: Michigan Forecast: Suddenly we go bone-dry in weather. Watch Torregrossa’s live weather update

stories.title: Michigan Funds $250K Study on Uterine Fibroid Services
stories.summary: The state will allocate $250,000.00 to commission a study evaluating options to expand detection, treatment, and awareness of uterine fibroids, with results to be reported within 30 days of receipt.

stories.title: Michigan Funds National Board Certification Incentives for Teachers
stories.summary: $2.5 million is allocated for National Board Certified teachers through a work project appropriation. Teachers receive $4,000 base awards with an additional $6,000 for those in Title I schools. The project aims to encourage certification and lapses unspent funds by September 30, 2029.

stories.title: Michigan Gas Prices continue climb while diesel sets new all-time record
stories.summary: The average diesel price in Michigan has reached $6.78, with some stations hitting $7, setting a new record. Rising oil prices and a refinery outage in Illinois are contributing to the increase, which also affects airfare and business operations.

photo.alt: Michigan Gas Prices continue climb while diesel sets new all-time record

stories.title: Michigan gas prices soar to $4.89, some Metro Detroit stations top $5
stories.summary: Gas prices in Michigan have risen to an average of $4.89 per gallon, with some Metro Detroit stations exceeding $5. Diesel fuel averages $6.67 per gallon, driven by global demand and a refinery outage in Illinois. The war in Iran has significantly contributed to the increase, nearly doubling the national average since February 28, 2026.

photo.alt: Michigan gas prices soar to $4.89, some Metro Detroit stations top $5

stories.title: Michigan got $173M to transform rural health. Where is it going?
stories.summary: Michigan is distributing $173 million in federal grants through the Rural Health Transformation Program to improve rural healthcare. Stakeholders argue the funds are insufficient to address Medicaid cuts and facility stability, with concerns that money is flowing to peripheral programs rather than hospitals. The state plans to allocate funds across four initiatives, but reporting transparency issues have emerged as budget deadlines approach.

photo.alt: State health officials discuss Rural Health Transformation Program progress with a Michigan House Appropriations Subcommittee on Sept. 22, 2026. (Eli Newman/Bridge Michigan)

stories.title: Michigan got $173M to transform rural health. Where is it going?
stories.summary: Michigan is distributing $173 million in federal Rural Health Transformation Program funds to improve rural healthcare through four initiatives: chronic condition collaboration, workforce preparation, home-based services access, and technology upgrades. However, rural healthcare leaders and legislators criticize the allocation as insufficient to address Medicaid funding cuts and operational strains, with concerns that the money is not reaching hospitals and critical areas. State officials reported $124.6 million allocated to 236 subrecipients as of September 2026, but lawmakers demand better transparency and performance metrics to ensure accountability.

photo.alt: a shot of the back of a seated woman testifying before a legislative committee.

stories.title: Michigan got $173M to transform rural health. Where is it going?
stories.summary: State officials and lawmakers highlight discrepancies in reported spending of $173 million allocated for rural health transformation, with concerns over transparency and funding timelines. The state must obligate funds by October 30 but can fully spend them until September 2027, raising questions about accountability and performance metrics.

photo.alt: St. Clair County rural health initiative

stories.title: Michigan governor race: Where candidates stand on school policy
stories.summary: Chris Swanson outlines a seven-point education plan prioritizing free school meals for all students, expanded preschool access, and directing state School Aid Fund to K-12 schools. He opposes replicating Mississippi's education model, arguing Michigan students are performing better than national test data suggests and advocating for an assessment of the state's education system if elected.

photo.alt: Michigan governor race: Where candidates stand on school policy

stories.title: Michigan House bill would give school credit for job experience
stories.summary: The bill would require school districts to grant credit to seniors who work at least 30 hours a week in manufacturing, construction, or other fields that provide verifiable job training.

photo.alt: Podcast title 'That's What They Say' with hosts Anne Curzan & Rebecca Hector

stories.title: Michigan House committee probes canvassing process amid dispute over citizen-only voting signatures
stories.summary: The Michigan House Select Committee on the Rules and Procedures of the State Board of Canvassers and the Bureau of Elections is investigating the canvassing process following the failure of a citizen-only voting initiative. The effort, which aimed to require citizenship verification for voting, was rejected on August 24 after a partisan deadlock on the Board of State Canvassers. Proponents plan to reattempt the initiative in 2028 and criticized the Bureau of Elections' signature validation process as unfair.

photo.alt: Image related to Michigan voting initiative

stories.title: Michigan Increases Insurance Provider Assessment Revenue by $7.414M
stories.summary: State restricted insurance provider assessment revenue, as appropriated in 2025 PA 22, is increased by $7,414,400. This adjustment boosts funding for insurance provider assessments in healthcare programs.

stories.title: Michigan is burning. Here’s what the next governor can do to extinguish the blaze.
stories.summary: The Detroit Regional Chamber has not endorsed either gubernatorial candidate, Jocelyn Benson or John James, due to their failure to secure a two-thirds majority vote from its PAC. The article argues that Michigan's next governor must prioritize education and economic development strategies to address the state's economic challenges, including boosting post-secondary credentials and transforming the state's economic development approach. The current gubernatorial race has been overshadowed by the U.S. Senate contest, with neither candidate adequately addressing long-term economic issues like workforce aging and talent retention.

photo.alt: U.S. Rep. John James, R-Shelby Twp., speaks at the Mackinac Policy Conference on Mackinac Island, Mich., on May 27, 2026. (Photo by Andrew Roth/Michigan Advance)

stories.title: Michigan Journalists of the Year
stories.summary: Jonathan Oosting and Mike Wilkinson were named Michigan Journalists of the Year for the fourth consecutive year. Their work exposed issues in Michigan's grant-making process, including a controversial $25 million health campus linked to a former House Speaker, and highlighted safety lapses at Michigan State University following a campus mass shooting.

stories.title: Michigan Launches Digital Credentialing Initiative for CTE Programs
stories.summary: $3 million is allocated for a statewide digital credentialing initiative supporting CTE programs. The program creates verifiable digital records of skills for students and educators to enhance workforce competitiveness through improved skills transparency and portability.

stories.title: Michigan launches project with crop insurance companies to reward regenerative farming
stories.summary: About 80 farmers in Michigan's thumb region will participate in a pilot project recognizing lower crop loss risks from regenerative farming techniques.

photo.alt: A grayscale image of a hand placing a ballot into a ballot box in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building, with trees in the background. The It’s Just Politics logo appears in the upper right corner.

stories.title: Michigan League of Handweavers’ biennial show in Ann Arbor will feature myriad disciplines
stories.summary: From weaving to doll-making, a broad range of craftsmanship will be featured in both exhibitions and public demonstrations at the Michigan League of Handweavers’ 23rd Biennial Fiber Show.

photo.alt: Michigan League of Handweavers’ biennial show in Ann Arbor will feature myriad disciplines

stories.title: Michigan Legislature Allocates $300 Million for Postsecondary Scholarship Fund in 2026 Budget
stories.summary: The Michigan Legislature has allocated $300 million for the postsecondary scholarship fund for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, with $200 million from the state school aid fund and $100 million from the general fund. The legislature intends for this fund to be the primary source for the Michigan achievement scholarship, aiming to increase annual deposits until fully implementing the scholarship's costs. If funding shortfalls occur, additional appropriations from the scholarship fund will be used, requiring notification to higher education committees.

stories.title: Michigan Legislature to Submit Joint List of Legislatively Directed Spending Items
stories.summary: The Michigan Senate and House must jointly submit a list of legislatively directed spending items within 30 days of the budget act's enactment. The list must include all publicly disclosed information about funded items, as required by the Management and Budget Act.

stories.title: Michigan Libraries Receive $750,000 for State Aid and eLibrary Expansion
stories.summary: $375,000 will be added to state aid for public libraries, with another $375,000 allocated for expanding the Michigan eLibrary's free online access to research materials. Funds will be distributed under the State Aid to Public Libraries Act.

stories.title: Michigan man among 7 named in Cornell fraternity sexual assault lawsuit
stories.summary: A St. Clair County, Michigan man and former Cornell University student is accused in a lawsuit of participating in the 2024 drugging and sexual assault of a female student at the Chi Phi fraternity house. The lawsuit, filed in September 2026, names seven individuals, Cornell University, and Greek organizations, alleging the victim was incapable of consent. The case has prompted a reopened criminal investigation by New York’s Tompkins County DA.

photo.alt: Gavel MLive

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Literacy Coaching and Intervention by 2027-2028
stories.summary: The state requires school districts to provide technical assistance for reporting pupil reading improvement plans by the 2027-2028 school year. District-identified literacy coaches must focus on intervention instruction rather than classroom teaching.

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Literacy-Focused Teacher Certification Test
stories.summary: The state requires the adoption of a teacher certification test ensuring elementary teachers can deliver evidence-based literacy instruction grounded in the science of reading.

stories.title: Michigan Mandates Precontract Risk Assessments for State Department Contractors
stories.summary: A new policy requires the department to conduct precontract risk assessments for financial, security, and insurance risks before executing contracts. A report on these assessments and executed contracts must be submitted by March 31, 2027.

stories.title: Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund Appropriation
stories.summary: For the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, $45,000,000 is appropriated for certain capital outlay projects from the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund. The adjusted gross appropriation remains at $45,000,000 with no interdepartmental grants, federal revenues, or local revenues specified.

stories.title: Michigan orchards are open. Where to find cider and donuts this fall
stories.summary: Michigan's apple orchards are in full swing, offering fresh cider, donuts, and fall activities. Visitors can enjoy picking apples and seasonal treats at various orchards across the state.

photo.alt: Michigan orchards are open. Where to find cider and donuts this fall

stories.title: Michigan parents got Facebook message saying son was lost. What video shows about his bus dropoff
stories.summary: Airport Community Schools Superintendent Ryan Duvall addressed an incident where parents received a Facebook message claiming their son was lost during a bus dropoff. The district filed a report with local law enforcement and emphasized that student transportation is managed by third-party vendor First Student, which retains responsibility for its employees. Administration is collaborating with First Student to review procedures and ensure driver protocols are followed, though the vendor has not yet responded to inquiries about preventive measures.

photo.alt: Michigan parents got Facebook message saying son was lost. What video shows about his bus dropoff

stories.title: Michigan Passes FY27 General Omnibus Appropriations Bill SB 878 PA 21 of 2026
stories.summary: Michigan's 103rd Legislature approved Senate Bill 878 on July 21, 2026, to make, supplement, adjust, and consolidate appropriations for state departments, agencies, and capital outlay purposes for fiscal years ending September 30, 2026, and 2027. The bill includes $135.6 million in adjusted gross appropriations for the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development for FY2027. Introduced by Senator Anthony, the act provides funding conditions and expenditure guidelines while repealing previous acts.

stories.title: Michigan PFAS Awareness Week is a call to action
stories.summary: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week highlights the dangers of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the state's environment and water supply. The week-long event, declared by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, encourages residents to reduce PFAS exposure while addressing new threats from data centers that use these chemicals. Advocates call for stricter regulations and corporate accountability to prevent further contamination.

photo.alt: Image related to PFAS awareness and water contamination

stories.title: Michigan progressive rabbis use Harris visit to press El-Sayed on 'nonnegotiable' Jewish concerns
stories.summary: A group of Michigan rabbis, part of Nonnegotiable Michigan, issued an open letter to Kamala Harris urging her to push Abdul El-Sayed to address Jewish safety and identity concerns. The rabbis criticized El-Sayed's stance on Israel and his campaign's association with Hasan Piker, requesting a meeting that he has yet to accept.

photo.alt: Kamala Harris and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan Provides Technical Assistance for Medicaid Mental Health Funding
stories.summary: At least $159,500 and 1.0 FTE position will support technical assistance for eligible districts to effectively use Medicaid funds for mental health services.

stories.title: Michigan Public names Brian Manzullo as managing editor of multiplatform news strategy
stories.summary: Michigan Public has appointed Brian Manzullo as its inaugural managing editor of multiplatform news strategy. Manzullo brings over 14 years of experience from the Detroit Free Press and The Arizona Republic to his new role, where he will strengthen the station's digital journalism and expand its reach across platforms. He will start on September 21, 2026, based in Ann Arbor.

photo.alt: Brian Manzullo headshot

stories.title: Michigan Public Service Commission Mandated to Provide Monthly Utility Rate Data
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission must submit a report by September 30 summarizing public hearings on utility issues and outages. It will also provide monthly utility rate data, reliability metrics, and complaint statistics online, including a dedicated webpage for pending rate cases with projected impacts for residential customers.

stories.title: Michigan rabbis push El-Sayed to change rhetoric on Israel, ensure safety of Jewish community
stories.summary: Michigan Jewish rabbis and leaders have launched Nonnegotiable Michigan, a coalition representing 40,000 Jewish voters, demanding Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed affirm commitments to Jewish safety, identity, and political participation. The group calls its demands an 'invitation' for El-Sayed to address concerns ahead of the Nov. 3 general election, as tensions rise over his rhetoric on Israel and Gaza. El-Sayed's campaign claims he is working to mend ties with the Jewish community through meetings and public commitments to safety.

photo.alt: Michigan rabbis push El-Sayed to change rhetoric on Israel, ensure safety of Jewish community

stories.title: Michigan-raised Nashville bluegrass artist sharing new album at The Ark show
stories.summary: Bluegrass artist Lindsay Lou will perform at an upcoming show in Ann Arbor on Oct. 4 at The Ark to share the release of her new album, Bluegrass Women. The album, released on Aug. 14, celebrates women's contributions to bluegrass and features collaborations with artists like Molly Tuttle and Sierra Hull. The show starts at 7:30 p.m. with tickets starting at $29.

photo.alt: Bluegrass artist Lindsay Lou will perform at an upcoming show in Ann Arbor on Oct. 4 at The Ark to share the release of her new album, Bluegrass Women. Photo provided by Sydney Griffin with permission to use.

stories.title: Michigan Reduces Quality Assurance Assessment Program Revenue by $1.978M
stories.summary: State restricted quality assurance assessment program revenue, as appropriated in 2025 PA 22, is reduced by $1,978,400. This adjustment affects funding for quality assurance programs in healthcare.

stories.title: Michigan regulators approve $74.5 million DTE Gas hike, less than half utility’s request
stories.summary: Michigan regulators approved a $74.52 million DTE gas rate hike Thursday — less than half of what the utility requested — raising typical residential bills by 3.34%, or $2.87 monthly, starting Oct. 1. Regulators blocked $284.1 million in costs tied to a compressor station project and require DTE to analyze racial disparities in service shutoffs.

photo.alt: Michigan regulators approve $74.5 million DTE Gas hike, less than half utility’s request

stories.title: Michigan regulators want to restrain utilities' bias toward building costly power plants
stories.summary: Governor Gretchen Whitmer asked the Michigan Public Service Commission for ideas on lowering utility bills. The commission says the most important way to do that is address 'capital bias.'

photo.alt: On the right, steam rises from the DTE Energy's Fermi 2 nuclear power plant. On the left in the distance the smoke stacks of the Monroe power plant. The USEPA's proposal would make such coal burning power plants capture 90 percent of greenhouse gas emissions.

stories.title: Michigan Releases 2026 Supplemental Funding Budget Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Technology, Management, and Budget has outlined new requirements in the 2026 supplemental funding budget, including annual work project account reporting, preferences for Michigan-made goods and veteran-owned businesses, in-person work policies, and space utilization assessments for state agencies. The provisions emphasize accountability, local economic support, and compliance with federal guidelines.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY2027 State Budget Details with Supplemental Funding Provisions
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for fiscal year 2027 includes provisions for policy change reporting, federal contingency funds, legacy cost allocations, and work project fund management. Key sections outline requirements for April 1 policy reports, $2.5 million in federal contingency authorization, and $133 million in pension-related legacy costs. The document also mandates preferences for Michigan-made goods and services in state expenditures.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill with Supplemental Funding for 2026
stories.summary: Michigan's FY27 General Omnibus Budget Bill allocates $34.7 million for pension-related legacy costs through 2027. The bill mandates exhausting existing work project funds before new appropriations, requires biannual work project account reports, prioritizes Michigan-made goods/services including veteran-owned businesses, enforces in-person work policies with 80% occupancy targets, and establishes space utilization assessments by July 1, 2027. It also promotes contracting with geographically disadvantaged businesses.

stories.title: Michigan Releases FY27 Supplemental Budget with $109.6 Million in Appropriations
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for Fiscal Year 2027 includes $109.6 million in supplemental funding across departments, including child care, Medicaid mental health services, and state police programs. The budget emphasizes compliance with federal regulations and reallocation of American Rescue Plan Act funds to ensure full expenditure by December 31, 2026. Provisions also address fiscal recovery fund management and audit requirements.

stories.title: Michigan reopens review of Line 5 tunnel permits following Supreme Court decision
stories.summary: Michigan regulators will reconsider permits for Enbridge’s Line 5 oil tunnel after the state Supreme Court ruled environmental impacts must be weighed before approval. Gov. Whitmer urged Enbridge to abandon the project, while tribes and environmental groups praised the decision.

photo.alt: Michigan reopens review of Line 5 tunnel permits following Supreme Court decision

stories.title: Michigan Repeals and Amends Sections of State School Aid Act of 1979
stories.summary: The text outlines the repeal of multiple sections from the 1979 State School Aid Act and the enactment of amendments. Some provisions take immediate effect, while others are scheduled for October 1, 2026. The act is ordered to take immediate effect under Article IV of the Michigan Constitution.

stories.title: Michigan Replaces Federal Funding Cuts for School Health Programs
stories.summary: Funds appropriated for adolescent and school health will replace federal funding reductions from the HHS-CDC and the state school aid act.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Grant Recipients to Submit Detailed Reports by September 1
stories.summary: The state mandates that grantees submit a report by September 1 of the current fiscal year, including audited financial statements, education and clinical quality data, trainee rosters, and Medicaid revenue by training site.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Medicaid Pharmaceutical Cost and Rebate Report by May 15
stories.summary: The department must submit a report by May 15 detailing Medicaid pharmaceutical costs, rebates, and related expenses for the previous fiscal year and first two quarters of the current year.

stories.title: Michigan Requires Updated Reading Assessments by August 2027
stories.summary: By August 1, 2027, school districts must update their reading assessments to include universal screening tools for dyslexia, minimizing instructional time impact through approved assessments.

stories.title: Michigan's 10th Congressional District Race
stories.summary: Coverage of Michigan's 10th Congressional District race, where voters in Macomb County will select a successor to Republican John James, includes an extended conversation with an Oakland University professor on civic dialogue.

photo.alt: Michigan's 10th Congressional District Race

stories.title: Michigan’s 96th House District race: Bridge issues dominate debate
stories.summary: Incumbent Republican Timmy Beson and Democratic challenger Chris Girard clashed over bridge access, tolls, and infrastructure during their debate for Michigan’s 96th House District. Beson emphasized local bridge funding and small business concerns, while Girard focused on affordability, cost-of-living challenges, and seeking state-level solutions for bridge control and oversight.

photo.alt: Timmy Beson, left, and Chris Girard, right.MLive graphic

stories.title: Michigan’s chronic absenteeism rate, once among the highest in the nation, falls for fourth year
stories.summary: The Detroit Public Schools Community District continued to see improvements in its chronic absenteeism rate, which was at 60% at the end of the 2025-26 school year.

photo.alt: Michigan’s chronic absenteeism rate, once among the highest in the nation, falls for fourth year

stories.title: Michigan's felony murder law disproportionately impacts Black residents
stories.summary: A new analysis reveals Black Michiganders are convicted of felony murder at three times the rate of white residents. The charge can apply when someone is involved in a crime where a death occurs, even if they weren't present. Advocates hope Michigan will follow Pennsylvania's lead in banning mandatory life sentences for felony murder.

photo.alt: Michigan's felony murder law disproportionately impacts Black residents

stories.title: Michigan's Food and Agriculture Investment Program Outlined in 2026 Supplemental Budget
stories.summary: The 2026 Supplemental Budget for Michigan's Agriculture Development Bureau establishes a Food and Agriculture Investment Program to expand the state's food sector, promote food security, and grow exports. The program will fund grants, infrastructure, and value-added agriculture projects with both state and external funds, requiring approval from the Michigan Commission of Agriculture and Rural Development. Unexpended funds remain available until September 30, 2029, to complete projects.

stories.title: Michigan's FY27 Budget Bill Includes New Reporting, Procurement, and Workforce Policies
stories.summary: The FY27 General Omnibus Bill (SB 878/PA 21 of 2026) establishes requirements for work project account reporting, prioritizes Michigan-made goods in state contracts, mandates in-person workforce policies, and requires space utilization assessments for state agencies. The bill also includes provisions for geographically disadvantaged business enterprises and federal policy impact reporting.

stories.title: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week Highlights Data Center Threats to Water Safety
stories.summary: Michigan's PFAS Awareness Week (Sept. 21-25) highlights the state's over 300 PFAS-contaminated sites and emerging threats from proposed data centers that could introduce new PFAS pollution through refrigerants and cable coatings. Clean water advocates are urging stronger regulations to address all PFAS chemicals and hold polluters accountable for cleanup costs, as low-income communities already burdened by legacy contamination face new risks.

photo.alt: A person holding a water sample with a droplet highlighting contamination concerns.

stories.title: Michigan’s sex offender registry shrank by nearly half. Here’s why.
stories.summary: A state supreme court ruling is sparking a major debate over constitutional rights and public safety as more than 20,000 sex offenders are being removed from Michigan’s registry. Michigan State Police have removed over 20,000 people from the registry following a landmark court decision that invalidated retroactive registration requirements for offenses before July 1, 2011.

photo.alt: Michigan’s sex offender registry shrank by nearly half. Here’s why.

stories.title: Michigan's Tenth Congressional race could determine which party controls Congress
stories.summary: The district, which represents parts of Macomb and Oakland Counties, has leaned Republican in the past, but the race between Michael Bouchard and Christina Hines is considered a toss-up.

photo.alt: democrat and republican

stories.title: Michigan's Tunnel of Trees is a fall favorite. Is it still detoured?
stories.summary: Michigan's Tunnel of Trees, M-119 between Harbor Springs and Cross Village, remains partially closed for repairs due to spring and summer runoff. Sections near Division Road and Devil's Elbow are detoured until 2027 and indefinitely, respectively, while one segment reopened recently. The scenic drive is a popular fall attraction despite current closures.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jenna Prestininzi

stories.title: Michigan’s two major party candidates for U.S. Senate offer differing ideas for health care
stories.summary: Republican Mike Rogers rolls out plan heavy on transparency; Democrat Abdul El-Sayed advocates for Medicare for All

photo.alt: Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers speaks to reporters at a campaign office in Taylor, Michigan on Saturday, September 19.

stories.title: Michigan’s Two Major Party Candidates for U.S. Senate Offer Differing Ideas for Health Care
stories.summary: The two U.S. senate candidates from Michigan offer vastly different ideas for health care. Lowering costs for consumers is the goal for both.

photo.alt: Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers speaks to reporters at a campaign office in Taylor, Michigan on Saturday, September 19.

stories.title: Michigan school districts, food pantries feel SNAP cut ripple effect ahead of cost shift to states
stories.summary: Across Michigan, school districts and food pantries are preparing for changes in SNAP benefits as states take on increased administrative costs starting October 1. Analysts estimate the shift will cost Michigan about $95 million in the first year, with over 167,000 residents, including 53,000 children, already losing SNAP benefits under H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed in July 2025.

photo.alt: Michigan school districts, food pantries feel SNAP cut ripple effect ahead of cost shift to states

stories.title: Michigan selects official Christmas tree for holiday season
stories.summary: Michigan has selected a 60-foot spruce donated by the Larry Riccio family from Iron Mountain as the state's official Christmas tree. The tree will be cut down on Nov. 5 and transported to the state Capitol in Lansing, where it will be prepared for a tree-lighting ceremony during the 42nd annual Silver Bells in the City celebration on Nov. 20.

photo.alt: Michigan selects official Christmas tree for holiday season

stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters' election history
stories.summary: Peters was first elected to the U.S. Senate in 2014, defeating Terri Lynn Land 55%-41%, and re-elected in 2020, defeating John James 49.9%-48.2%.

photo.alt: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters' election history

stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters to join USC political center. When he starts
stories.summary: Michigan Senator Gary Peters, known for his political career spanning local and state offices, is set to join the USC political center. The article outlines his history, including roles in the Rochester Hills City Council, Michigan State Senate, and U.S. Congress. Specifics about his new position at USC are not detailed in the provided text.

photo.alt: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters to join USC political center. When he starts

stories.title: Michigan Sen. Gary Peters to lead USC political center. What he'll do
stories.summary: After completing his Senate term in January 2027, U.S. Sen. Gary Peters will co-lead one of the only political centers in the country jointly led by a Democrat and a Republican. Peters will become the Carmen H. and Louis Warschaw Endowed Chair in Practical Politics at the University of Southern California and serve as director of the Center for the Political Future at the USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences alongside Republican strategist Mike Murphy.

photo.alt: Portrait of Jalen Williams

stories.title: Michigan Senate seat up for grabs between former state rep, local party chair
stories.summary: Voters in Michigan Senate District 15 will elect a new state senator in the Nov. 3 general election. The race pits former state representative Felicia Brabec (D-Pittsfield Township) against Republican Jason Rogers, chair of the Washtenaw GOP. Both candidates qualified after primary elections in August, with Brabec defeating fellow Democrat Michael White and Rogers running uncontested. Current term-limited Sen. Jeff Irwin (D-Ann Arbor) is not seeking re-election.

stories.title: Michigan seniors share secrets to living to 100
stories.summary: Michigan centenarians shared their secrets to living to 100 during a ceremony at a luncheon. They emphasized enjoying life and having fun, while Canton Township Supervisor Anne Marie Graham-Hudak presented proclamations to the honorees. The event highlighted their roles as family members, caregivers, and community contributors beyond being historical witnesses.

photo.alt: Michigan centenarians celebration event

stories.title: Michigan Sheriffs’ Association to Receive $85K for Victim Support
stories.summary: $85,000.00 will be awarded to the Michigan Sheriffs’ Association for victim support and trainings.

stories.title: Michigan Smart Trade Alliance tracker shows over $26 billion in tariff-driven costs paid statewide
stories.summary: The Michigan Smart Trade Alliance has launched a tracker estimating Michigan households have incurred over $26 billion in tariff-related costs since January 2025, or about $6,419 per household. The estimate uses data from the National Taxpayers Union Foundation, though other analysts and the White House provide lower figures. The alliance advocates for ending trade policies they claim raise costs and hinder economic planning.

photo.alt: Michigan Smart Trade Alliance tracker shows over $26 billion in tariff-driven costs paid statewide

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Director to Ensure Expenditure of Fiscal Recovery Funds by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director must ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are expended by December 31, 2026. Funds at risk of lapsing after September 30, 2026, will be automatically reappropriated for the same purpose through December 31, 2026.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Includes New Work Project Reporting and Procurement Requirements
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget for FY27 includes provisions requiring annual reports on work project accounts, prioritizing Michigan-made goods and services, enforcing in-person work policies, and assessing federal policy impacts. Agencies must submit space utilization assessments by July 2027 and optimize office space usage. The budget also mandates reporting on federal guidelines affecting department operations by December 2026 and June 2027.

stories.title: Michigan State Budget Requires Expenditure of ARPA Funds by December 2026
stories.summary: The state budget director must ensure all American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds allocated to Michigan under Public Law 117-2 are fully expended by December 31, 2026. Funds that would otherwise lapse after September 30, 2026, are automatically reappropriated for the same purpose until the deadline.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Complete Space Utilization Assessment by July 1
stories.summary: The Michigan state department is required to complete a space utilization assessment by July 1 using a form developed by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget. The assessment will cover all space assigned under building occupancy agreements and leased office locations, with plans to optimize space usage.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Prioritize State-Owned Facilities in Space Optimization
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must develop a plan to reduce, consolidate, or optimize assigned space, prioritizing state-owned facilities. The plan must comply with space standards established by the Department of Technology, Management, and Budget unless exceptions are approved.

stories.title: Michigan State Department to Report on Federal Policy Impacts by December 31, 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan state department must submit a report by December 31, 2026, detailing federal guidelines, rules, or policy changes (including H.R. 1 and the Rural Health Transformation Program) that significantly impact its operations. The report will address changes in federal revenue and their effects on public health and welfare.

stories.title: Michigan State Fiscal Recovery Funds Expenditure Plan
stories.summary: The Michigan state budget director is required to ensure all state fiscal recovery funds from the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021 are spent by December 31, 2026. Unexpended funds after September 30, 2026 will be automatically reappropriated until that deadline. The act also outlines reallocation procedures for funds at risk of missing deadlines, including redirecting them to public health and safety employee payroll and benefits.

stories.title: Michigan state House committee hears testimony over concerns about ballot initiative process
stories.summary: A state House committee in Michigan is examining ways to improve the ballot initiative process after a conservative-backed measure failed to qualify for the ballot. Americans for Citizen Voting (ACV) submitted over 700,000 signatures but was disqualified due to insufficient valid signatures, with the group criticizing delays and lack of transparency in the review process. The committee emphasized it is focused on procedural improvements rather than political outcomes.

photo.alt: Petition

stories.title: Michigan State Lodge FOP endorses Chedrick Greene for 35th Senate District
stories.summary: The Michigan State Lodge Fraternal Order of Police announced their endorsement of state Sen. Chedrick Greene (D-Saginaw) in his re-election bid to represent Michigan’s 35th Senate District.

stories.summary: Michigan State’s medical school is handling a sexual assault case following a decade of difficult self-reflection on its policies and procedures.

stories.title: Michigan State University classes go remote after ‘unprecedented’ outage
stories.summary: Michigan State University moved most classes to remote instruction following a widespread power outage on Sept. 19 that left buildings without hot water. President Kevin M. Guskiewicz called the situation 'unprecedented' and said restoration could take up to a week, with 24 buildings requiring additional cleanup.

photo.alt: Michigan State University

stories.title: Michigan State University shifts to online classes after power outage
stories.summary: Michigan State University has transitioned to online instruction and remote work through Sept. 21, 2026, following a power outage that disrupted hot water and other services on the East Lansing campus. The outage began when a central connection point at the T.B. Simon Power Plant failed, prompting university leaders to reduce strain on systems while crews work to restore services. President Kevin M. Guskiewicz emphasized the university's priority of community safety and wellbeing during the ongoing response.

photo.alt: An sign at one edge of the Michigan State University campus on Monday, Aug. 17, 2020 in East Lansing. (Jake May | MLive.com)

stories.title: Michigan State University shifts to online classes after power outage
