stories.title: Michigan Strategic Fund looks to future of battery, auto parts supply industry
stories.summary: The Michigan Strategic Fund revised incentives for battery maker Our Next Energy, reducing state funding from $200 million to $150 million and adjusting job commitments and timelines. The company has shifted focus to grid storage and defense contracts amid EV market challenges. The fund also expanded a program to support auto parts suppliers in transitioning to EV and diversified supply chains.

photo.alt: Auto factory

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court blocks proof-of-citizenship voting measure
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court blocked a November ballot measure requiring proof of citizenship to vote, but voters will decide on a proposal to restrict utility spending on political campaigns. Fact-checks are available to help voters understand the issues.

photo.alt: A city street is littered with debris and wet with rain. A street sign reads 'Charlevoix' in the foreground.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court candidates compete for two seats
stories.summary: The League of Women Voters hosted a non-debate forum for six Michigan Supreme Court candidates competing for two seats in the November 3rd election. Candidates discussed judicial experience, legal philosophy, and systemic issues like resource disparities in court staffing and access to legal representation.

photo.alt: Michigan Hall Of Justice Supreme Court Building In Lansing

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court orders review of Oxford school shooter's life without parole sentence
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has directed a review of Ethan Crumbley's life without parole sentence for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting.

photo.alt: A grayscale image of a hand placing a ballot into a ballot box in front of the U.S. Supreme Court building, with trees in the background. The It’s Just Politics logo appears in the upper right corner.

stories.title: Michigan Supreme Court sends Oxford school shooter case back to appellate court for review
stories.summary: The Michigan Supreme Court has remanded Ethan Crumbley’s case back to the Court of Appeals to review whether a lower court erred in sentencing him to life without parole for the 2021 Oxford High School shooting. Crumbley, who pleaded guilty in 2022 to four murders and seven injuries, had his appeal to withdraw his guilty plea denied in May 2025 for lacking merit. His attorney argued that waiving appellate rights by pleading guilty deprived him of a direct appeal.

photo.alt: Memorial items on the sign of Oxford High School in Oxford, Mich., with dates referencing the 2021 shooting incident.

stories.title: Michigan Tax Tribunal to Hire 2.0 Limited-Term Employees for Small Claims Backlog
stories.summary: The Michigan Tax Tribunal will hire up to 2.0 limited-term employees to address a backlog in small claims cases. Unexpended funds will remain available until project completion by September 30, 2029, with a total estimated cost of $359,300.

stories.title: Michigan Technological University H-STEM Project Cost Reduction
stories.summary: The cost to construct the Michigan Technological University – H-STEM Engineering and Health Technology Complex – Phase I project has been decreased by $1,514,800 to a new total project cost of $51,585,200. The state building authority share is $29,699,800, with the university contributing $21,885,200 and the state general fund/general purpose share at $200.

stories.title: Michigan to Implement Career and Technical Education Reporting Mechanism
stories.summary: The Michigan Department of Education will develop a reporting system for school districts to track career and technical education participation and workforce development outcomes. The report will include student participation numbers, high school course enrollment, and postsecondary program enrollment data.

stories.title: Michigan to Publish Literacy Achievement and Opportunity Transparency Dashboard by March 1, 2027
stories.summary: Michigan's legislature mandates the publication of a literacy achievement and opportunity transparency dashboard by March 1, 2027. The dashboard, to be developed by the department in collaboration with the department of lifelong education and the center, will track metrics like pre-K access, educator training in reading science, curriculum usage, and literacy assessment results from M-STEP and SAT tests.

stories.title: Michigan to Update Dyslexia Handbook Every 5 Years
stories.summary: The state mandates regular reviews and updates of the Michigan Dyslexia Handbook or a similar resource guide, with updates not exceeding a 5-year interval to ensure alignment with current research on dyslexia education.

stories.title: Michigan Townships Association Joins Coalition Opposing Proposal 1 of 2026
stories.summary: The Michigan Townships Association joined a bipartisan coalition urging voters to reject Proposal 1 of 2026, which would initiate a constitutional convention to rewrite Michigan's Constitution.

photo.alt: Michigan political roundup image

stories.title: Michigan universities slide in rankings in new national report
stories.summary: The University of Michigan dropped from 20th to 25th in national rankings, with nearly half of 12 listed Michigan institutions seeing declines. Smaller institutions improved their standings, while MIT unseated Princeton as the top-ranked university. The rankings now consider affordability, earnings by major, and post-graduation income levels.

photo.alt: Michigan universities slide in rankings in new national report

stories.title: Michigan Uses Mobile Dental Permit Fees to Offset Costs
stories.summary: Revenue from mobile dental facility permit fees will be used to offset the costs of processing and issuing permits. This directive is based on public health code provisions.

stories.title: Michigan villages have a fix for shortage of officials. Townships can’t use it
stories.summary: Michigan’s rural communities are struggling to find people to hold public office. Lansing has been slow to help.

photo.alt: Issues Watch returns Sept. 30 to discuss Michigan rural government crisis

stories.title: Michigan villages have a fix for shortage of officials. Townships can’t use it
stories.summary: Michigan villages can appoint non-resident clerks and treasurers to address staffing shortages, while townships are legally required to elect officials from within their borders. Over 75% of townships and villages struggle to fill mandatory positions, with some facing crises in election management and tax collection. Two bills aimed at easing these issues have stalled in the Legislature.

photo.alt: The Michigan Treasury helped Village of Garden President Jeffrey Lefevre switch the community’s clerk and treasurer jobs from elected to appointed roles.

stories.title: Michigan voters to decide on constitutional convention proposal
stories.summary: Michigan voters will vote on Proposal 1 to decide whether to call a constitutional convention in Lansing. This question appears on the ballot every 16 years since 1978, with past rejections. If approved, a spring election would select delegates for a fall 2027 convention.

photo.alt: Michigan voters to decide on constitutional convention proposal

stories.title: Michigan Weather: Below-normal temps will keep a grip until warmup arrives
stories.summary: Michigan is experiencing below-normal temperatures with frost advisories in the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula. Highs are expected in the low to mid 60s through Wednesday, with a warmup to the 70s by the weekend. Light rain is possible in southern Michigan, while beach hazards persist along Lake Michigan and Lake Huron.

photo.alt: High temperatures map for Michigan on Tuesday from National Weather Service

stories.title: Michigan Weather: Cool, dry air settles in for the week
stories.summary: A mostly dry week with cooler temperatures is expected, with Monday forecast to have the coldest temps and potential frost in parts of the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula. Temperatures will remain in the 60s through midweek before gradually warming to the 70s by late week and next weekend. The National Weather Service highlights a cooler, drier pattern from Canadian high pressure, with frost risks and falling humidity creating a fall-like feel.

photo.alt: An aerial view of Tahquamenon Falls State Park’s Upper Falls and 1,100-foot boardwalk and viewing platform in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. In May the park opened the new fully accessible boardwalk replacing an old staircase that leads to the landing of Michigan’s largest waterfall.

stories.title: Michigan will be red, orange and yellow soon. 2026 foliage forecast
stories.summary: Michigan's fall foliage in 2026 will feature a range of colors from red, orange, and yellow, depending on the tree species. The article details how different trees, such as maples, aspens, oaks, and hickories, contribute to the vibrant autumn palette across the state's Upper Peninsula, northern Lower Peninsula, and southern regions.

photo.alt: Michigan fall foliage color map for 2026

stories.title: Michigan woman, 63, pleads to 5 charges of sexually assaulting girl she babysat
stories.summary: A 63-year-old Midland County woman pleaded no contest to five counts of second-degree criminal sexual conduct with a relation, resulting in a one-year jail sentence and 25 years of sex offender registration. The charges stem from abuse between 2013 and 2020 when she babysat a girl under 13. Prosecution dismissed 48 other counts in exchange for her plea.

photo.alt: The Midland County Courthouse in downtown Midland.Cole Waterman

stories.title: Michigan woman accused in $4.6M child modeling scheme sentenced to 5 years in prison
stories.summary: Chanise Coyne, 46, of New Boston, was sentenced to five years in prison for wire fraud related to a $4.6 million scheme involving fictional child modeling events. She also faces paying $4.67 million in restitution and three years of supervised release. Authorities allege she used funds for personal expenses, including Taylor Swift concert tickets and gambling.

photo.alt: Judge gavel, scales of justice and law books in court

stories.title: MichMash: Analyzing Michigan's gubernatorial race ahead of the midterms
stories.summary: With only months until the midterms, Michigan's gubernatorial candidates are seeking support, but the race between Jocelyn Benson and John James is drawing less attention than the U.S. Senate race. Andrea Bitely of Bitely Communications calls it 'the most boring gubernatorial race in history,' noting that Mayor Mike Duggan's May 21, 2026, withdrawal reduced interest. Bitely suggests candidates need more rallies and a compelling message to engage voters, with elections set for November 3.

photo.alt: MichMash: Analyzing Michigan's gubernatorial race ahead of the midterms

stories.title: MichMash: Do Michigan voters want to rewrite the state’s constitution?
stories.summary: Michigan voters will decide in the November 3 midterm elections whether to hold a constitutional convention in 2026. The proposal has drawn opposition from diverse groups, including the UAW, Michigan Chamber of Commerce, Planned Parenthood, and the Michigan Catholic Conference, who argue it could create instability and uncertainty.

photo.alt: MichMash: Do Michigan voters want to rewrite the state’s constitution?

stories.title: MichMash: Top 10 Michigan House seats that could flip in the 2026 midterms
stories.summary: The episode discusses key races to watch in the 2026 Michigan midterms, focusing on 10 House seats that could flip parties. Analysts note the national political climate, including an unpopular Republican president, may influence local elections, requiring politicians to work harder to retain their seats.

photo.alt: MichMash: Top 10 Michigan House seats that could flip in the 2026 midterms

stories.title: Midland County Sheriff’s deputy pleads guilty after crashing Jeep with BAC of 0.157
stories.summary: A Midland County Sheriff’s deputy has admitted in court to being impaired by alcohol when he crashed his Jeep while off-duty. Joseph C. Shuler, 29, pleaded guilty to driving while visibly impaired on Sept. 15, with prosecutors dismissing a more serious operating while intoxicated charge.

photo.alt: Midland County Sheriff’s deputy pleads guilty after crashing Jeep with BAC of 0.157

stories.title: Midland County Sheriff’s deputy pleads guilty after crashing Jeep with BAC of 0.157
stories.summary: A Midland County Sheriff’s deputy has admitted to being impaired by alcohol when he crashed his Jeep while off-duty. Joseph C. Shuler, 29, pleaded guilty to driving while visibly impaired on Sept. 15, leading to the dismissal of a more severe charge. The crash occurred on June 16 with a blood-alcohol content of 0.157, well above Michigan's legal limit of 0.08.

stories.title: Midland's Tridge could be replaced. What city is doing
stories.summary: Midland city officials are starting to plan for the replacement of the city's three-span 'Tridge' that's become an iconic landmark. The Midland City Council voted in August to begin design work for a new version of the structure. City Manager C. Bradley Kaye indicated replacement could occur in 2028 with estimated costs of $8-10 million.

photo.alt: Portrait of Dan Basso

stories.title: Midland says Tridge will be replaced. When it could happen
stories.summary: The city of Midland plans to replace the Tridge, a wooden bridge structure. Previous renovations in 2017 included restaining, replacing decking, railing, and adding LED lights, costing $2.7 million. Current efforts focus on studying the timeline and cost for a full replacement.

stories.title: Mike Dawes
stories.summary: Mike Dawes, an English guitarist renowned for his creative fingerstyle techniques and ability to perform multiple parts on a single guitar, will be featured at The Ark. His work includes viral videos, popular arrangements, and collaborations with mainstream artists like Justin Hayward of The Moody Blues.

stories.title: Mike Duggan Drops Out of Michigan Governor's Race
stories.summary: Independent candidate Mike Duggan, former Detroit mayor, has withdrawn from the gubernatorial race with less than six months until the midterm elections. Analysts suggest the current political climate made an independent victory unlikely, despite Duggan's perceived electability. The decision impacts both Democratic and Republican reactions as the race narrows.

photo.alt: Mike Duggan Drops Out of Michigan Governor's Race

stories.title: Mike Greene says the $261 ticket he got for speeding 10 miles over the limit in a school zone was uncalled for.
stories.summary: Mike Greene is contesting a $261 speeding ticket in a school zone, arguing that the lack of proper signage led to his violation. Authorities maintain the ticket was justified, stating that drivers remain in the school zone until an 'end' sign is seen. Greene claims the city is prioritizing revenue over child safety by not installing adequate signs.

photo.alt: Police pull over a driver in a school zone

stories.title: Mike Rogers calls for gas tax pause. It’s a no-go, says state GOP leader
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers proposed suspending state and federal gas taxes amid rising fuel prices, but Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall, a GOP ally, warned it would jeopardize a bipartisan road funding deal and state budget stability. Gas prices in Michigan have surged to $4.75 per gallon on average, with some stations exceeding $5, as conflicts in the Middle East disrupt oil supplies. Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed criticized Rogers' proposal, attributing price spikes to the Trump administration's policies.

photo.alt: Michigan’s $4.75-per-gallon average gas price is the 10th highest in the U.S., with some stations in metro Detroit exceeding $5 per gallon.

stories.title: Mike Rogers calls for gas tax pause. It’s a no-go, says state GOP leader
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers proposed suspending state and federal gas taxes amid rising fuel prices, but Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall, a GOP ally, warned it would jeopardize a bipartisan road funding deal. Rogers criticized recent gas tax increases, while Hall defended the 2026 bipartisan agreement that shifted fuel tax revenue to road repairs. High gas prices in Michigan, currently averaging $4.75 per gallon, have sparked debate over tax suspensions and their impact on infrastructure funding.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers, Republican U.S. Senate candidate, speaks about gas tax issues in Michigan.

stories.title: Mike Rogers Claims He Was An Assembly Line Worker, The UAW Said That Is Stretching The Truth
stories.summary: Mike Rogers claimed he worked as an assembly line worker at Cars & Concepts in Michigan, but the UAW disputes this, stating the facility was an aftermarket shop rather than a traditional assembly line. UAW Local 651 president Art Reyes II emphasized that the work at Cars & Concepts involved modifying pre-built vehicles, not building them from scratch, and criticized Rogers for misrepresenting his experience to connect with Michiganders' automotive heritage.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers Claims He Was An Assembly Line Worker, The UAW Said That Is Stretching The Truth

stories.title: Mike Rogers outlines plan to lower health care costs in Metro Detroit
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers proposed a health care cost reduction plan focused on price transparency and expanding the Trump Rx program to lower prescription drug costs. He argues transparency in medical pricing will empower patients to shop for affordable care.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers outlines plan to lower health care costs in Metro Detroit

stories.title: Mike Rogers voted against children’s health coverage over and over
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers repeatedly voted against expanding health insurance for low-income children, opposing legislation that Michigan officials said could help tens of thousands of uninsured kids get medical care. Between 2004 and 2009, the then-congressman cast 19 votes against measures to extend, expand, or increase funding for the State Children’s Health Insurance Program. The program aimed to cover children in working families who earned too much for Medicaid but not enough for private insurance.

photo.alt: Mike Rogers and children's health care policy

stories.summary: Republican US Senate nominee Mike Rogers is highlighting his 14-year congressional career, focusing on national security, healthcare, and bipartisan work, while facing criticism from Democratic rival Abdul El-Sayed over his Trump ties and policy stances. Rogers, who previously ran for Senate in 2024, now seeks to replace retiring Sen. Gary Peters, emphasizing his bipartisan background and policy proposals like expanding shop classes and affordable housing.

stories.title: Milling, paving work on McKinley Road in Flushing area to take place over 4-day period
stories.summary: A contractor will mill and pave a stretch of McKinley Road between Nashua Trail and Vienna Road in Flushing Township from Sept. 24 to 27, 2026. The road will remain open with flaggers directing traffic, and motorists are urged to drive cautiously and allow extra travel time.

stories.title: Millions still needed to install air conditioning throughout district
stories.summary: While Detroit Public Schools Community District (DPSCD) anticipates most schools will have air conditioning within two years, 11 schools will have partial AC and eight will receive none due to funding gaps. The district needs an additional $245 million to fully equip these schools, with budget discussions planned for the fall or early winter. Board member Monique Bryant highlighted issues with late notifications for school closures, affecting parents' childcare arrangements.

stories.title: MLive announces its print newspapers will move fully online starting in December
stories.summary: MLive has announced that all of its print newspapers will be discontinued and moved fully online, with the final print editions published on December 6, 2026. The decision follows data showing digital subscriptions have surpassed print, and the company emphasizes the move is to better serve readers and communities. MLive will not lay off newsroom staff and acknowledges some readers may not transition to digital due to lack of internet access.

photo.alt: A framed newspaper article at the building once known as the Protesting Christian Reform Church on South Park Street in Kalamazoo.

stories.title: MLive axes print edition, reflecting changing local media landscape

The decision, attributed to declining print readership and economic pressures, will result in job losses but not at their Ohio printing facility. Experts and community members expressed concerns about the loss of physical news engagement and the future of local journalism.

stories.summary: A Genesee County judge ruled that LakeVille Community Schools must release a 2016 investigation into former middle school teacher Matthew Chapin to MLive-The Flint Journal. The decision comes after a legal battle to unseal records related to the teacher charged with sex crimes.

stories.title: More focus on career pathways for high schoolers
stories.summary: DPSCD will roll out its high school redesign this fall, with ninth graders at 11 neighborhood high schools exploring career pathways through a seminar class to guide their course selection. The initiative includes smaller class sizes, additional tutoring for literacy support, and hiring seven more counselors to achieve a 1:250 student-to-counselor ratio. Superintendent Nikolai Vitti emphasized reducing credit deficits to enable college and career course access by 11th grade.

stories.title: More research is needed on solutions to partial-day absenteeism
stories.summary: Parents in Detroit express mixed reactions to a new policy addressing unexcused early sign-outs, with concerns about socioeconomic barriers and students with disabilities. stories.title: More team teaching on tap in Michigan schools
stories.summary: Team teaching, where multiple teachers collaborate in the classroom, is expanding in Michigan. The Michigan Educator Workforce Initiative has supported 15 schools in recent years, with 16 more joining for the 2026-27 school year. The program provides structures and tools to help teachers improve student achievement and retention.

stories.summary: The Detroit school district is using its facility master plan to significantly improve its buildings, including adding air conditioning to many of them.

stories.summary: The winners of the 2026 Pythagorean Prize were celebrated for their achievements in mathematics. The prize highlights students who have demonstrated exceptional skill and dedication to the subject.

stories.title: Near Sleeping Bear Dunes, residents battle beavers — and feds — over floods
stories.summary: Residents around Little Traverse Lake in Leelanau County blame beaver dams for recurring flooding that damages properties. The National Park Service only permits dam removal after water levels peak, but residents argue this is too late to prevent damage. A $1.1 million culvert project and studies show dam removal can significantly lower lake levels, yet the park maintains a cautious approach requiring data-driven justification for interventions.

photo.alt: A beaver dam

stories.title: Negative Space at Detroit Artists Market: An Exhibition of Unrealized Public Sculpture
stories.summary: Negative Space is an exhibition at Detroit Artists Market exploring unrealized public sculptures through maquettes, renderings, and documentation. Curated by Veronica Bielat, it highlights how public space is shaped by both realized and rejected works, featuring artists like Foster Willey, Lois Teicher, and Richard Bennet whose proposals never materialized but demonstrate artistic process and resilience.

stories.title: Nessel discusses threats of federal monitors, law enforcement at polling places during voter forum
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel addressed federal threats to election processes during a voter forum in Washington, D.C., emphasizing preparations for potential federal interventions at polling places and the impact on local election officials. She highlighted Michigan's decentralized election system and efforts to combat misinformation and threats against election workers, alongside fellow Democrats from California and Maine.

photo.alt: Nessel discusses threats of federal monitors, law enforcement at polling places during voter forum

stories.title: Nessel said Michigan is ready for threats against election officials
stories.summary: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel discussed threats of federal monitors and law enforcement at polling places during a voter forum, highlighting Michigan's role as a focal point for Trump's 2020 election challenges. She emphasized the state's decentralized election processes and preparedness through units like hate crimes investigations and briefings for local law enforcement.

photo.alt: Panelists speak during the Center for American Progress’ 2026 Midterm Elections forum. stories.title: ‘Never doubt your humanity’: UMich kicks off Latine Heritage Month
stories.summary: The University of Michigan celebrated the start of Latine Heritage Month with an event themed 'Lo Futuro,' featuring speeches from Hector Galvan and Curtis Acosta. The ceremony highlighted cultural preservation, immigration challenges, and the vibrant history of Latine communities. Over 150 students and community members attended the opening at the Michigan Union.

stories.title: New bills would require Michigan utilities to pay customers for long outages
stories.summary: Senate Democrats introduced bills requiring Michigan utilities to pay outage credits to customers after outages exceeding 72 hours or four annual outages. The bills aim to discourage prolonged outages and bar utilities from recouping credits through rate hikes, following storms that left 300,000+ households without power.

stories.title: New Deepfake Resilience Hub combats rise of AI-generated misinformation
stories.summary: The University of Michigan's new Michigan Deepfake Resilience Hub (M-DRH) aims to help the public detect and understand AI-generated misinformation. Led by Khalid Malik, the initiative addresses gaps in deepfake detection tools for everyday users and includes a public verification portal, training programs, and policy guidance. The project was selected for a grant from the University's Strategic Initiative Fund, a $1 billion investment over 10 years.

stories.title: New ‘Kids Count’ data shows drop in college readiness, education participation among young adults
stories.summary: The Michigan League for Public Policy's 2026 Kids Count report shows declining college readiness and education participation among young adults, with Michigan ranking 42nd nationally in education. The report highlights increased poverty rates for children, drops in Medicaid and SNAP enrollment, and rising food insecurity, while noting an 84% increase in youth voter turnout since 2016.

stories.title: New pipe repair method lets homeowners skip the dig
stories.summary: Homeowners facing damaged sewer lines can now opt for a less invasive repair method called sewer lining, which avoids the need for excavation. Marcus Piwonski of Hoover Electric, Plumbing, Heating and Cooling explains that the technique uses a felt-type liner inverted into existing pipes, creating a new pipe within the old one. This method spares homeowners the disruption of digging and is recommended for early detection of issues through camera inspections.

stories.title: New Ypsi farmers and gardeners added to library’s oral history project
stories.summary: The Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Project has expanded with 12 new narrators and 11 oral histories, focusing on BIPOC, Indigenous, younger, immigrant, and refugee growers in the Ypsilanti area. The project documents their stories about food sovereignty, cultural legacy, and community resilience, including contributions from Anishinaabe seed-keeper Shiloh Maples and refugee advocate Phimmasone Kym Owens. A new community advisory board helped deepen representation, and the collection will be available through the Ypsilanti District Library until Sept. 28.

photo.alt: A panel discussion at an opening reception at the Ypsilanti District Library’s Superior Branch for the expansion of the Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Project. Project interviewees Julius Buzzard, Kyunghee Kim, Akaiia Hill, and P. Deisha Myles are pictured left to right.

stories.title: Nonprofit awarded $20K grant to build new water trailhead at Southwest Detroit park
stories.summary: A local nonprofit working to establish a network of water trails and greenways on the Lower Rouge River has been awarded a $20,000 grant to build a new trailhead at Fort Street Bridge Park in Southwest Detroit. The multi-purpose trailhead, expected to open in fall 2026, will serve as a respite for paddlers and advance the organization's 29-mile water trail plan across 10 Wayne County communities. An additional $8,400 grant will fund safety signage and volunteer training for logjam management.

stories.title: North America’s first Swedish swim-up sauna opens in Michigan
stories.summary: North America’s first Swedish swim-up sauna has opened at Mount Bohemia's Nordic Spa in Michigan. The spa complex also includes hot springs, steam rooms, and other Nordic-inspired amenities.

stories.title: Northern Michigan lawmaker calls for stricter penalties on lake sturgeon poaching
stories.summary: A northern Michigan lawmaker has introduced legislation to increase fines for illegally taking or possessing lake sturgeon, a threatened species. The bill, House Bill 6409, would raise maximum penalties from $2,000 to $5,000, following a reported incident of a six-foot sturgeon being dumped in Muskegon County. Lake sturgeon, which can live up to 150 years, are protected under state law with strict fishing restrictions.

stories.summary: A Saginaw man was charged with first-degree home invasion and multiple assault counts after allegedly breaking into his girlfriend's home with a firearm, threatening to kill residents, and dragging her by the hair. Police pursued the suspect following a domestic dispute, leading to a crash near Linwood. He faces a $750,000 bond and has a prior felony firearm conviction.

stories.title: Saginaw man gets prison time for stabbing, trying to kill man at East Side gas station
stories.summary: A Saginaw man is prison-bound for repeatedly stabbing and trying to kill a man at an East Side gas station in an apparent dispute over childcare. Saginaw County Circuit Judge Darnell Jackson on Thursday, Sept. 17, sentenced 52-year-old Donald A. Williams to five to 15 years in prison. He gave Williams credit for 301 days already served in the county jail and ordered him to pay $198 in fines and costs.

stories.title: Saginaw man pleads guilty to child abuse for ‘whooping’ minor over sexual orientation
stories.summary: A Saginaw man, Tony H. Morgan, 53, pleaded guilty to third-degree child abuse for allegedly beating an underage girl with a belt because she identified as gay. Prosecutors stated Morgan forced the girl to undress, struck her repeatedly, and made derogatory remarks about her sexual orientation. As part of a plea deal, Morgan will receive probation and must complete a parenting class.

stories.summary: Voters will elect a new majority to the Detroit school board this fall, an election that could shape the future of Michigan’s largest district for years to come. The race for five open seats comes as parents and community members push for improvements in early literacy scores, facilities, and administrative transparency. With only two incumbents running and many candidates criticizing current leadership, observers worry a new board could stall or reverse recent academic gains.

stories.title: This powerful breakfast challenges what it means to be a man, preventing violence against women

stories.title: This stargazing destination will become a refuge for migrating birds, expert says
stories.summary: The Keweenaw Peninsula in Michigan, with its dark skies, is becoming a critical refuge for migrating birds. Researchers from Michigan Technological University are banding birds to study migration patterns and ecosystem health. Associate professor Jared Wolfe highlights the area's role in supporting nighttime migrators like northern yellow warblers and red-eyed vireos, while addressing threats like light pollution.

stories.title: This year’s budget does not fill a longtime gap in funding for Michigan English learners
stories.summary: Michigan's public schools face structural deficits in funding for English learners, with over 104,200 students enrolled in the 2024-25 school year. Advocates argue that increased funding could help students transition out of specialized programs faster and improve academic outcomes. While lawmakers aim to gradually increase ELL funding to match 2021 recommendations, no timeline has been set for achieving these goals.

stories.summary: Tribal leaders and environmental advocates gathered in Lansing to oppose Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline, emphasizing concerns about potential oil spills in the Great Lakes and the proposed tunnel project's impact on sacred sites. stories.summary: Trinity Health Ann Arbor has launched a program to restore natural areas and trails on its campus, aiming to provide a stress-relieving space for patients and staff while addressing environmental concerns. The initiative focuses on managing stormwater runoff, particularly salt from winter use, to protect the Huron River. The hospital emphasizes a holistic approach to health, integrating community well-being and workforce support through habitat restoration and education.

stories.title: Trinity Health layoffs expose the danger of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
stories.summary: Trinity Health in Livonia, Michigan announced 557 layoffs linked to federal Medicare and Medicaid cuts from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). The law has already put 23 Michigan healthcare providers at risk and is projected to strip 171,000-355,000 residents of health coverage. Republican lawmakers including Senate candidate Mike Rogers and Michigan's congressional delegation supported the legislation despite its negative impacts.

stories.title: Trump administration says developers, loggers can kill endangered species
stories.summary: The Trump administration’s top wildlife official issued a directive expanding rollbacks of endangered species protections, allowing developers and loggers to kill endangered animals if the activity’s purpose is not to kill them. Wildlife advocates warn this undermines the Endangered Species Act, creating loopholes for habitat destruction and accidental harm. Legal challenges and debates over the law’s interpretation are expected to intensify.

stories.title: Trump lowers fuel economy standards. Detroit automakers welcome change
stories.summary: The Trump administration introduced relaxed fuel economy standards, which Detroit automakers support but environmental groups criticize. The new rules reduce requirements for vehicle efficiency, aligning with Trump's opposition to electric vehicle incentives. The standards project a 2031 fleet average of 34.9 mpg, down from Biden-era projections, and are expected to lower vehicle costs while increasing carbon emissions.

stories.title: Trump lowers fuel economy standards. Detroit automakers welcome change
stories.summary: The Trump administration has finalized new fuel economy standards that relax requirements for automakers, reducing the mandated mileage compared to previous projections. The change aligns with Trump’s campaign to roll back policies favoring electric vehicles, potentially increasing vehicle affordability but also exposing Americans to more pollution. The decision follows tensions with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz, which impacted oil prices.

stories.title: Warren man fatally struck while teaching daughter to drive, police say

The crash occurred in the 24000 block of Warner Avenue around 4 p.m., with emergency responders transporting him to a hospital where he later died. Police state drugs and alcohol were not factors, and the daughter is cooperating with investigators.

photo.alt: Jenny Sherman headshot

stories.title: Warren Parks Commission Seeks Additional Sponsorships for Drone Show
stories.summary: The Parks and Recreation Commission discussed sponsorship support for event expenses and identified a need for additional funding to proceed with an advertised drone show. Commissioners recommended pursuing more local business sponsorships to address the funding gap.

stories.title: Washtenaw Business Lens: How AI is transforming the way people do business
stories.summary: Jonah Bailey and Andy LaBarre discuss AI's impact on industries like manufacturing, healthcare, and software, emphasizing the need for guardrails, ethical considerations, and the urgency for businesses to adapt. They highlight challenges in customer behavior prediction, data center sustainability, and AI-generated content transparency.

photo.alt: Jonah Bailey discussing AI in business

stories.title: Washtenaw County awards 9 mini grants to local community organizations
stories.summary: Washtenaw County’s Office for Community and Economic Development awarded $40,000 to nine local businesses as part of the Mini Grant Program in 2026.

stories.title: Washtenaw County weighs landfill expansion, Northville residents object
stories.summary: Northville Township residents oppose GFL’s proposed Arbor Hills Landfill expansion in Salem Township due to past pollution and unapproved height increases. Washtenaw County is weighing waste reduction against landfill space needs, with further discussion scheduled for Nov. 18.

photo.alt: Washtenaw County weighs landfill expansion, Northville residents object

stories.title: Washtenaw Housing Alliance introduces the 'Yvonne Fund' to assist those assisting the homeless
stories.summary: The Yvonne Fund, a permanent endowment, provides ongoing financial support for permanent supportive housing services in Washtenaw County. By distributing annual grants to organizations like Avalon Housing and Michigan Ability Partners, the fund aims to reduce reliance on yearly fundraising and ensure long-term stability for housing initiatives. The model has already supported 65 housing units in 2026 through $326,000 in grants.

photo.alt: A general image related to housing initiatives

stories.title: Washtenaw United: Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation continues its philanthropy in uncertain times
stories.summary: The Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation discusses its community-driven grant-making process, local impact investing strategies, and the generational impact of scholarships. Shannon Polk highlights how community members review applications, data-informed decisions, and stories of scholarship recipients transforming lives in Washtenaw County.

photo.alt: Shannon Polk, President and CEO of Ann Arbor Area Community Foundation

stories.title: Washtenaw United: SafeHouse Center continues to serve those recovering from domestic violence with help from the community
stories.summary: SafeHouse Center's Executive Director Christine Watson discusses the organization's role in supporting domestic violence survivors, challenges with affordable housing, and the importance of community partnerships. Watson emphasizes the need for continued investment in resources to ensure survivors can transition safely from temporary shelter to stable housing and community integration.

photo.alt: Christine Watson, Executive Director of SafeHouse Center

stories.title: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan works to prepare grants for its partners that serve the community
stories.summary: United Way for Southeastern Michigan evaluates grant impact through mid-year and final reports, with 72% of funds used for staff salaries and benefits. Organizations face challenges like funding cuts and burnout, but collaboration among service providers is growing. The partnership with WEMU explores community investments in equity and opportunity.

stories.title: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan presents Power of the Purse 2026
stories.summary: United Way for Southeastern Michigan's Power of the Purse 2026 event focuses on supporting women's financial stability and independence. Senior Director Katie Groves discusses the initiative's role in providing grants to women-led organizations, addressing systemic barriers, and offering wraparound services to over 424 families in Washtenaw County. The event highlights the historical struggle for women's financial autonomy, tracing back to the 1974 Equal Credit Opportunity Act.

photo.alt: Washtenaw United: United Way for Southeastern Michigan presents Power of the Purse 2026

stories.title: Washtenaw United: Washtenaw Housing Alliance Introduces the 'Yvonne Fund'
stories.summary: The Washtenaw Housing Alliance is one of many groups working in our community to end homelessness in Washtenaw County. The latest tool in its mission is the Yvonne Fund, which is designed to create lasting systemic solutions to homelessness.

photo.alt: Norman Herbert and Madeline Garcia representing the Yvonne Fund at the Timko Broadcast Center.

stories.title: Wayne County judge Cusick dismisses Detroit Tenants Union lawsuit
stories.summary: A Wayne County judge dismissed the Detroit Tenants Union's lawsuit against the 36th District Court. The union claimed judges allowed landlords to collect rent or evict tenants from properties lacking city-issued certificates of compliance. The dismissal follows Mayor Mary Sheffield's announcement to bring thousands of rental properties up to code within a year.

stories.title: Wayne County man accused of shooting, killing girlfriend during argument
stories.summary: Damarco Darnell Manns, 31, was charged with second-degree murder and other offenses after allegedly shooting and killing his girlfriend, Frances Beatty, 28, during an argument in Van Buren Township. The incident occurred on September 17, and Manns was denied bond during his September 21 arraignment. He is scheduled for a probable cause conference on September 29.

stories.title: WB I-696 at Woodward reopens following motorcycle crash
stories.summary: Westbound I-696 at Woodward reopened Wednesday morning after a motorcycle crash. The Michigan Department of Transportation reported the crash and closure at 7:12 a.m. on Sept. 23, with ramps from I-75 also closed during the investigation. The freeway and ramps reopened just before 10 a.m., and the motorcyclist is expected to recover.

stories.summary: Washtenaw Community College (WCC) received the 2025 Environmental Excellence Partnership Program Award in the Waste Reduction and Recycling category from the Washtenaw County Water Resources Commissioner’s office. stories.summary: The Muslim Student Association at WCC hosted a Ramadan Annual Iftar event to foster community connections through faith and education. The event featured discussions about Ramadan's spiritual significance, including Laylatul Qadr, and aimed to educate non-Muslim students while supporting Muslim peers balancing academics with religious observance.

stories.title: West Michigan airport receives state grant for safety improvements
stories.summary: West Michigan Regional Airport has secured a $152,540 grant from the Michigan Department of Transportation to enhance safety operations through updated runway markings and snow removal equipment. The funding will repaint runway markings and purchase a plow truck to address seasonal wear and improve winter maintenance. The airport will also apply retroreflective glass beads to improve visibility during nighttime and poor weather conditions.

Peters represented Michigan's 9th and 14th Congressional Districts from 2009 to 2015.

stories.title: When do leaves change colors in Michigan? Where leaves are turning now
stories.summary: Michigan's diverse tree varieties each have unique fall color patterns, according to Michigan State University Extension. In the Upper Peninsula and northern Lower Peninsula, maple trees turn orange and red, while quaking aspen and larch trees produce yellow leaves. Southern Michigan features red oaks with subtle red leaves and sassafras with yellow to deep red foliage.

stories.title: When does daylight saving time end in 2026?
stories.summary: Unless Congress acts, daylight saving time is scheduled to end at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift provides an extra hour of sleep but results in earlier sunsets during winter. The change is unlikely to affect Halloween, as it occurs after the holiday on Oct. 31.

stories.title: Whitmer directs MSP to investigate fatal crash following ICE pursuit in Grand Rapids
stories.summary: Gov. Gretchen Whitmer has directed the Michigan State Police to investigate a fatal car crash in Grand Rapids that occurred when Mario David Coronado Juárez, a father of three, fled a traffic stop involving U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents. The crash, which happened around 7:10 a.m. on Sunday, resulted in Coronado Juárez’s death after his vehicle caught fire upon hitting a tree. Local activists and officials, including U.S. Rep. Hillary Scholten, have called for transparency and accountability, with community members demanding justice and an end to ICE-related violence.

stories.title: Who will be exempt from Medicaid work rules in Michigan? What to know
stories.summary: The first wave of Michiganders affected by stricter Medicaid work rules, about 5,000 immigrants, will lose routine coverage on Oct. 5, 2026, transitioning to emergency-only benefits. Changes requiring 650,000 Michiganders to work 80 hours monthly or provide excuses for exemptions begin in January 2027. State officials are preparing systems to manage the overhaul, including hiring 400+ navigators and allocating $12.25 million in grants for local organizations.

stories.summary: Residents of Lincolnshire Village Apartments in Canton report unsafe conditions including mold, electrical issues, and water damage, seeking assistance from elected officials. A tenant who paid for her own mold test claims management dismissed her concerns and issued lease violations leading to an eviction. U.S. Rep. stories.title: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?
stories.summary: Michigan's judicial elections separate incumbent judges into their own ballot sections under a 1982 law lobbied for by sitting judges. This practice allows incumbents to avoid competing directly with challengers, a system critics argue insulates judges from political pressures while proponents claim it protects judicial independence. The law was championed by former state Rep. Virgil C. Smith, who defended it as necessary to shield judges from 'the predatory nature of the political system.'

photo.alt: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?

stories.title: Why daylight saving time is suddenly back in the spotlight
stories.summary: The debate has gained new attention after Trump publicly urged senators to approve the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent and eliminate the twice-yearly clock changes. The House approved the bill in July, but its fate in the Senate remains uncertain. With less than three months until clocks are set to 'fall back,' lawmakers are running short on time if they hope to change the system before Nov. 1.

stories.title: Why does the U.P. have a volcanic ridge?

photo.alt: A picture from Eagle Harbor in the Upper Peninsula. The large green ridge you see in the background is the Greenstone Flow, which forms the spine of both the Keweenaw Peninsula and Isle Royale. The 'fingers' of black rock you see extending into Lake Superior are also lava flows--though much smaller--that were the 'last gasps' of the Midcontinent Rift System.

stories.title: Will clocks fall back on Nov. 1? Here's the latest

stories.title: Will Comerica Park be renamed?
stories.summary: The fate of Comerica Park, home to the Detroit Tigers, has drawn significant public attention as Fifth Third and Comerica's merger raises questions about a potential name change. While Fifth Third Park is a possibility, a decision will be made in the offseason after evaluation. Detroit Tigers' Davis acknowledges the public's interest in the park's legacy.

photo.alt: Will Comerica Park be renamed?

stories.title: Will this be the last time we 'fall back'? Trump pushes end to DST
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is advocating for a permanent end to Daylight Saving Time, but legislation to achieve this faces uncertainty in Congress. The Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 requires Senate approval and Trump's signature, but Senate leadership has questioned its viability. If the bill fails, DST will end on Nov. 1, 2026, at 2 a.m.

photo.alt: Daylight Saving Time clock change illustration

stories.title: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?
stories.summary: Trump has long supported ending the twice-yearly clock changes, calling the practice 'foolish, inconvenient' and costly. He argues for permanent daylight saving time, citing benefits like fewer traffic accidents and energy savings. The House approved the Sunshine Protection Act in July, but its Senate fate remains uncertain as lawmakers race to act before Nov. 1.

photo.alt: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?

stories.title: Wisconsin DNR orders Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work
stories.summary: Wisconsin’s DNR ordered Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work near Iron County after an Aug. 25 spill. The agency cited a pattern of noncompliance, including unauthorized wetland disturbance, and may pursue enforcement action. Enbridge claims it’s working on cleanup and the bypass simultaneously.

photo.alt: Wisconsin DNR orders Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work

stories.title: Wixom Lake water level raised early by Four Lakes Task Force
stories.summary: The Four Lakes Task Force began raising the water level on the Tobacco River side of Wixom Lake on Sept. 19, moving up work that was originally scheduled for spring 2027.

photo.alt: Wixom Lake water level raised early by Four Lakes Task Force

stories.title: Woman fatally stabbed in Downtown Detroit, suspect in custody
stories.summary: A woman in her 30s was fatally stabbed Sunday afternoon near the intersection of Woodward Avenue and E. Congress Street in Detroit. The suspect, a man in his 40s, was chased and captured by police using surveillance cameras. Authorities are investigating the motive, as no prior interaction between the victim and suspect was reported.

photo.alt: Detroit Police Department cruisers parked at the scene of a fatal stabbing near the intersection of Woodward and E Congress. (WDIV)

stories.title: Woman sentenced for false bomb threat at Lansing’s public transit center
stories.summary: A woman was sentenced to three years of probation for making a false bomb threat to Lansing's Capitol Area Transit Authority. Nefateria Denise Ferguson, 32, called in the hoax at 8:10 a.m. on April 22, 2025, and later admitted it was a prank. The court emphasized the serious consequences of such threats, which disrupted public order and required emergency responses.

photo.alt: Gerald R. Ford Federal Building

stories.title: Woman stabbed to death while on lunch break in Downtown Detroit was attacked at random, family says
stories.summary: Jaquoya Wix, 34, was fatally stabbed in an alley near Woodward Avenue and E Congress Street in Downtown Detroit on Sept. 20 while on her lunch break at Chipotle. Her family confirmed the attack was random, and the suspect is in custody.

photo.alt: Woman stabbed to death while on lunch break in Downtown Detroit was attacked at random, family says

stories.title: Women in Tech returns to a2Tech360 on Monday
stories.summary: Ann Arbor SPARK’s 'a2Tech360' is underway with a series of events planned over the course of the 10-day event celebrating innovation in the greater Ann Arbor region. Jennifer Hayman is Senior Vice President of Marketing, Communication & Events for Ann Arbor SPARK, and she talked to Caroline MacGregor about the 'Women in Tech' event lined up for Monday, September 28th from 10 AM-3 PM.

photo.alt: The 'Women in Tech' event as part of a2Tech360.

stories.title: Work Project Appropriation for GSRP Outreach Campaign
stories.summary: The 2024-2025 outreach and enrollment campaign funding is designated as a work project appropriation. Unexpended funds will carry forward into 2025-2026, with the project's estimated completion date set for September 30, 2027.

stories.title: Worker dies in construction accident near downtown Grand Rapids
stories.summary: A worker at a construction site near downtown Grand Rapids died Tuesday, Sept. 22, after being struck by a backing truck.

photo.alt: Worker dies in construction accident near downtown Grand Rapids

stories.title: Workers uncover human remains in Newaygo County. MSP says no foul play
stories.summary: Police say human remains were found on a construction site in Newaygo County on Sept. 21, 2026, but officials don't believe a crime was committed. The remains were discovered in the 7300 block of Croton Hardy Drive near the Croton Dam Pond, and the Western Michigan University Medical Examiner’s Office has taken custody for examination.

photo.alt: Workers uncover human remains in Newaygo County. MSP says no foul play

stories.title: WWE Nxt Makes Its Fox Theatre Debut November 14
stories.summary: WWE NXT will debut at the Fox Theatre in Detroit on November 14, 2026, marking a new event for the venue.

stories.title: Yo-Yo Ma performs Lord of the Rings halftime show with Michigan Marching Band
stories.summary: Grammy Award-winning cellist Yo-Yo Ma joined the Michigan Marching Band for a Lord of the Rings medley during a halftime show to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the franchise’s first film. The performance was a collaboration between the marching band and Ma, marking a special event at the football game.

stories.title: Yoga and goats go together at this farm in metro Detroit
stories.summary: Maybury Farm in Northville, Michigan, has been offering yoga sessions since May with live goats as an added twist. The sessions, held every Saturday at 10:30 a.m., attract participants seeking a fun and interactive wellness experience. The farm, open to the public since 1975, hosts sold-out weekends with registration required 48 hours in advance.

stories.title: Ypsilanti Grub Crawl Ypsitasty Coming Soon
stories.summary: Ypsitasty, a 15th-anniversary food crawl, will take place in Downtown Ypsilanti, Cross Street, and Depot Town on September 29, 2026, from 4 to 8 p.m. Local restaurants will offer bites while businesses stay open late to welcome attendees. Diane Keller of the Ann Arbor/Ypsilanti Regional Chamber emphasized the event's role in showcasing community offerings through food and shopping.

photo.alt: Ypsitasty is in its 15th year, taking place Downtown Ypsilanti, Cross Street and Depot Town.

stories.title: Ypsilanti Grub Crawl Ypsitasty Coming Soon
stories.summary: Ypsitasty celebrates its 15th year on Tuesday, Sept. 29, from 4 to 8 p.m. The popular grub crawl takes place in Downtown Ypsilanti, Cross Street and Depot Town, with local restaurants offering tasty bites and other businesses staying open late to invite attendees to stop in.

stories.title: Ypsilanti library closes after patron reports bedbug near computer bank
stories.summary: The Ypsilanti District Library's Michigan Avenue branch closed on Sept. 12, 2026, after a patron reported a bedbug near the computer bank. Trained dogs inspected the area but found no additional bedbugs, leading to reopening on Sept. 15. The library closed again on Sept. 19 for precautionary treatment due to increased bedbug activity in the area.

stories.summary: The River Street Anthology, a project documenting local music scenes in Ypsilanti, received $30,000 in grant funding this year. The support will help expand the project's reach beyond the local community.

stories.title: YpsiTasty returns to Ypsilanti, showcasing local restaurants and businesses
stories.summary: YpsiTasty, a food-focused event organized with the A2Y Regional Chamber, returns to Ypsilanti on Sept. 29. The annual event allows participants to sample dishes from local restaurants and explore downtown businesses while supporting the community. Now in its 15th year, the event features a trolley service, special offers, and tickets ranging from $10 to $25 depending on age and student status.

photo.alt: YpsiTasty returns to Ypsilanti, showcasing local restaurants and businesses

stories.title: YpsiTasty returns to Ypsilanti, showcasing local restaurants and businesses
stories.summary: YpsiTasty, an annual grub crawl event in Ypsilanti, is set to return on Sept. 29, 2026. The event highlights local restaurants and businesses, featuring a chalkboard advertisement at a participating establishment. Organized with support from the A2Y Chamber of Commerce, the crawl aims to celebrate the community's culinary scene.
